title: ExxonMobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: PATRICK MULVA
affiliation: VICE PRESIDENT OF INVESTOR RELATIONS & CORPORATE SECRETARY, EXXON MOBIL CORPORATION
speaker: Exxon
text:
Good morning. I'd like to cover several aspects of today's meeting. First, as we typically note at the outset of similar meetings, any estimates, plans and projections discussed today by Mr. Raymond and Mr. Tillerson are forward-looking statements.  

Actual results, including research recoveries, volume growth, capital expenditures, and project outcomes could differ materially, due to the factors they will discuss and those noted under the caption, "Factors Affecting Future Results," on our Internet site.  

I also refer you to the frequently used terms, posted on our Web site, which include definitions of some of the key financial and operating measures, we will use today, and the additional information required by SEC Regulation G.  

I'd like to take this opportunity to familiarize everyone with the safety features of this auditorium. In case of an emergency, we will be notified through the public address system. Emergency exits, as shown on the screen above me, are situated at the rear of the auditorium, where you entered, and down in front on either side.  

To ensure that the meeting is conducted in the interest of all shareholders, there are certain rules of conduct governing this meeting. These rules were posted on signs at the entrances to this meeting, are included in the program, and are shown on the screen above me. Let me reiterate several of the rules.  

The distribution of pamphlets and other literature, banners, signs and other displays is strictly prohibited in this hall. Anyone who intentionally obstructs or interferes with this lawful meeting by physical action or verbal utterances is in violation of Texas law.  

Any persons engaging in such conduct will be asked to seize; and, if they refuse, they will be escorted from the meeting.  

So we can be fair to the speakers and other shareholders, please turn off all cell phones and pagers, during the meeting.  

Only shareholders as of the record date of April 5th or their properly appointed proxies are entitled to speak at this meeting.  

To ensure as much as possible that all shareholders who want to address the meeting today have the opportunity to do so, we ask you to follow these additional instructions. First, if you want to speak for a proposal, go to the audience microphone on your right; conversely, go to the microphone on your left to speak against a proposal. It is our intent to provide an equal opportunity to speak for all of our shareholders, present today, by allowing speakers on both sides of the issues equal access to the microphones.  

We ask that you respect this and make your comments from the appropriate microphone. If you're not at the proper microphone, we will turn off the microphone and ask you to proceed to the appropriate one. If you wish to make comments, you must first fill out a speaker identification card that is available at the stand behind the microphone.  

After you've completed this card, give it to the attendant and proceed to the microphone. This card confirms that you meet the requirements to speak at this meeting.  

Additionally, the meeting will be conducted in English. Shareholders making comments, during the meeting, must speak or have their words translated into English so that the majority of shareholders present can understand what is being said. Additional time will not be give for translation.  

Speakers who do not comply will have their microphone turned off. We recognize -- when recognized by the chairman, begin by stating your name; unless otherwise provided in these rules, you may speak for up to two minutes. There will be separate discussion periods for all the 11 business items at today's meeting.  

After all business items have been voted on, there should be some time for general comments and questions. As noted in the proxy statement, the chairman has broad authority to conduct the meeting in an orderly and timely manner.  

Due to the number of items on today's agenda and our need to conclude the meeting within a reasonable period of time, discussion on individual items of business will generally be limited to 10 minutes. We cannot assure that every shareholder, who wishes to speak, will be able to do so.  

We ask speakers to keep their comments brief and limited to the specific item of business under consideration at that time. Speakers who raise another topic will be asked to hold their comments until the appropriate time. We would not permit comments that are offensive or otherwise inappropriate.  

We would also ask that any issues of personal interests that are not relevant to all shareholders be raised directly with the appropriate company representatives outside of the annual meeting.  

The sponsor of a shareholder proposal will have up to four minutes to present the proposal. No second to the motion is required. The sponsor may reserve a portion of formants to give concluding comments.  

Additional time will not be provided. Time permitting other shareholders, who wish to speak about management or shareholder proposals, may have two minutes each, when recognized by the chairman.  

As we have done in the past, we have provided a timing system with lights that will show speakers the amount of time they have spoken and when their time has expired. I'd like to now demonstrate the system at this time. When the chairman recognizes the speaker at one of the microphones, a green light will come on at the display on both sides of the stage and at both speaker stands.  

However, the microphone will be activated, only if the speaker stands, where the speaker has been recognized by the chairman. The time remaining for each speaker is displayed at the speaker stands.  

When the speaker's time remaining reaches 30 seconds, a yellow light will turn on.  

A red light and multiple beeps will indicate the speaker is at the end of the time allowed, and the microphone would be turned off.  

One other matter was noted in the proxy and the program given to each of you. The laws of New Jersey, where Exxon Mobil is incorporated, provide that no business can be brought up for a vote, unless proper notice has been given to all shareholders.  

Therefore, in fairness to other shareholders and in keeping with the laws to govern our annual meeting, formal business at today's meeting is restricted to the items included in this year's proxy statement.  

Additional proposals may not be introduced from the floor. Reentry into the hall will be limited to intervals between items of business. Ushers will advise when reentry is permitted. In addition, for safety reasons, please do not stand in isles or at the back of the hall and do not block the access.  

Thank you.

title: ExxonMobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: LEE RAYMOND
speaker: Exxon
text:
I would, now, like to make a few comments about our business results. Since last year, there continues to be a considerable turmoil in the Middle East, and the instability in Iraq persists.  

There has been a rising public concern over the current level of oil and gasoline prices and the potential for supply shortages. At the same time, we are seeing strengthening economic growth in many parts of the world. In the midst of this changing environment, your company continues to deliver industry-leading results; and we remain positive on our future prospects.  

Your company had another outstanding year in 2003. We continued to be the envious industry leader in safety performance, and had the lowest number of safety incidents in the history of the company. We set a record with earnings of $21.5 billion, and we again led the industry with a return on capital employed of 21%. We generated a strong cash flow of almost $31 billion.  

We continued to advance profitable growth opportunities. Our capital investments for 2003 totaled $15.5 billion.  

We maintained our commitment to deliver value to shareholders. Last year, your company returned a record $11.5 billion to shareholders through dividend payments and share purchases.  

In 2003, we also made significant progress in a number of key initiatives. In the upstream, we more than replaced reserves for the 10th consecutive year. We started up 16 key upstream projects around the world.  

Our downstream earnings nearly tripled versus 2002, and our chemical business had their best earnings in the last five years. Our global functional organization continues to deliver cost efficiencies and revenue enhancements.  

In 2003 alone, these initiatives totaled more than $2 billion before tax exceeding our expectations.  

As you can see, all segments of our business made strong contributions to the continuing success of the company in 2003. At Exxon Mobil, the safety and health of our employees, contractors and the people, who live and work near the areas where we operate, is paramount.  

Our industry-leading safety performance continues; and, once again, your company set a record for the fewest safety incidents in 2003. Despite this achievement, we will continue this focus on safety to achieve our goal that nobody gets hurts.  

It has been five years since the merger of Exxon and Mobil. Some have identified the merger as one of the few clearly successful mega mergers, if not the most successful. Since we reappraised all of our investment decisions, so it's appropriate to look at our performance during this period.  

Since the merger, we have generated over $120 billion in cash. We have invested roughly 66 billion, or about 55%, to improve our base business and to provide profitable growth opportunities. We have retained approximately 10% to increase our flexibility to add attractive future investments.  

We also distributed $47 billion to you -- our shareholders. To put this in context, our shareholder distributions alone in the last five years exceeded the market capitalization of 98% of the companies currently trading on the New York Stock Exchange.  

Your company earned $74 billion in the past five years. This represents the combined earnings of nearly 400 of the companies in the S&P 500 over the same period. We have captured $10 billion in synergies and efficiencies as well as added 9 billion oil equivalent barrels to our industry-leading reserves base.  

In summary, I think, the facts speak for themselves on what the merger has meant to the shareholders. Exxon is dedicated to creating long-term sustainable value in growth to shareholders. In the past five years, we've returned $47 billion to shareholders through a combination of dividend payments and share purchases. These distributions provide a total yield of 4.9% in 2003.  

Our average dividend yields in the last five years by itself, substantially, exceeded the average of the 50 largest US corporations. Our compound annual dividend growth rate of 4.7%, over the past 20 years, outpaced the 3.1% growth in the US Consumer Price Index. Exxon Mobil's track record of increasing the dividend payments each year is unmatched among international oil companies.  

Last month, we extended this record to 22 years with an 8% increase in quarterly dividend payments.  

Exxon Mobil's unparalleled commitment to proprietary technology development and application differentiates us from our competitors and does provide a competitive advantage.  

Our technology leadership is evident across the entire company. You were able to see many examples of our technological innovations, earlier this morning, at the displays in the lobby. In the upstream, we support technology initiatives covering exploration through enhanced recovery and field depletion applications. This emphasis on technology opens new frontiers for cost-effective resource developments - deeper water, arctic regions, and other challenging environments.  

A good example is our Sakhalin-1 project in Russia, where we have drilled horizontal reaches in excess of 5 miles. This extended reach drilling permits drilling of development wells from onshore locations versus costlier and more difficult offshore structures.  

In the downstream and chemicals, we are leveraging technology to improve our manufacturing processes and to meet drilling market needs for new products. For example, molecular management allows us to combine industry-leading technologies in both molecular fingerprinting and process modeling along with real-time optimization tools to select the slated crudes for refinery in our network that will provide the highest margin opportunity.  

Our proprietary research in chemicals has led to the development of industry-leading new chemical and catalysts in products. We remain committed to investment in proprietary research, and we continue to invest at levels above all of our competitors.  

We consider technology the lifeblood that provides your company with the tools to compete increasingly difficult environments and to meet new product demands. We strongly believe that the role of science and technology in this industry is absolutely vital, if we are to provide reliable and affordable energy supplies.  

Your company is committed to superior corporate citizenship. Our goal is to help meet the world's drilling energy needs in an economically, environmentally and socially responsible manner. We have long valued the importance of maintaining the highest ethical standards and business integrity in our corporate governance practices.  

We continue to be an industry safety leader, and we will continue our unrelenting focus on workplace safety. The company is equally vigilant when it comes to product safety and the health of those, who buy our products and live in the communities, where we do business.  

Exxon Mobil is taking a number of actions, as we have for many years, to improve efficiency in energy and reduce emissions. We continue to implement energy savings steps at our facilities and invest in new cogeneration projects.  

We also have projects underway to increase the supply of cleaner burning natural gas. We conduct research in advanced fuels in vehicle systems.  

Our investments in the global climate and energy project at Stanford University is aimed to accelerate the development of commercially viable energy technologies that can dramatically increase efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions on a worldwide scale. Wherever Exxon Mobil operates, we make positive social and economic contributions to strengthen local communities.  

Exxon Mobil recognizes the significant human and economic toll of the global health pandemics -- malaria, HIV AIDS, and tuberculosis in sub-Saharan Africa -- and the emerging threat they pose in China, India and Latin America. We understand the impact of pandemics on our employees, their families, and our operations. We are actively funding and collaborating with local and international efforts to fight these diseases and improve public health.  

Our recently published Third Annual Corporate Citizenship Report provides a broad perspective on the many social, economic and environment issues, in which our company is engaged, and our actions related to those issues. The report is available in the lobby, via mail, and on the Web site. While today's world continues to change, the principles of good corporate citizenship do not. We are proud of our performance and are committed to ongoing improvement.  

You, as investors, know that any investment decision carries with it the consideration of risk and reward. Conventionalism would suggest that higher risk should yield higher reward; and, conversely, lower reward should follow lower risks. However, as is many adages of our business, we don't always except them. That's particularly true, when you look at the total return of our shares over the last two decades.  

Over the past 20-year period, Exxon Mobil stock has earned nearly a 16% per year return. That alone is equal to a better than any other investment you see on this chart. But as you can also see, your company has accomplished this with far lower risk than our competition and at the same level as the entire S&P 500. I think it is fair to say there aren't many companies if any that can provide shareholders with that kind of track record.  

We had another outstanding year at Exxon Mobil, and the facts speak for themselves. Consistency, discipline, and a rigorous approach to everything we do are the hallmarks of Exxon Mobil.  

Our relentless focus on operational excellence and our global functional organization continued to deliver results to the bottom line. While our competitors may seek to copy our approach, it is not something that is easily replicated.  

We do what we say we are going to do, and we measure our performance in a consistent and transparent way. We have the financial flexibility to grow our business where it makes sense; however, we will not grow for growth sake, but only when we are convinced that we are building long-term shareholder value. In the coming decades, meeting the expected increase in global energy demand will require a broad portfolio of energy options; and hydrocarbon fuels are expected to remain a dominant energy source through, at least, the middle of this century.  

Your company will play a central role in taking on the challenge to provide the vital energy supplies needed for economic growth in both developed world and in developing countries.  

Now, let's look at what's taking on the world's toughest energy challenges means to the men and women of Exxon Mobil, and after the video, Rex will take us through a more detail business review of the Company.  

(VIDEO PRESENTATION)

title: ExxonMobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: REX TILLERSON
speaker: Exxon
text:
Good morning. As you just saw, the world's demand for energy is expected to rise another 40% by the year 2020. Meeting the tough challenges of satisfying this growing demand is what Exxon Mobil is all about. As Lee already mentioned, your company accomplished another solid performance in 2003. Each of the business segments registered strong performance this past year.  

Upstream earnings of $14.5 million were record. We produced 4.2 million oil equivalent barrels of liquids and natural gas a day and added 2.1-billion oil equivalent barrels to our industry-leading resource base. We continued to progress our portfolio of profitable upstream development opportunities. Major projects now underway or in the planning stages are expected to develop up to 25 billion net oil equivalent barrels. We anticipate about 30 startups in the next three years with many on resource-rich areas, such as West Africa, Qatar, The Caspian and Russia.  

Our downstream earnings were the second highest ever. In North America, our low sulphur motor fuels investment program is nearly complete with one remaining project expected to start up this year.  

We continued our relentless focus to control costs and deliver on revenue enhancement initiatives. We captured over $1.5 billion of efficiencies in the downstream alone. Our chemical business had their best earnings in five years and achieved sales matching the record levels of 2002.  

Looking first at the upstream. The geographic diversity of our portfolio provides us with a competitive advantage. In 2003, we produced 4.2 million oil equivalent barrels per day from our current asset base. This includes 60,000 productive wells and 1,800 fields in nearly 600 offshore platforms in 25 countries.  

Our reserve replacement totaled to 105% of production including the effects of property sales. This marks the 10th year in a row of crude reserve additions have more than replaced our produced volumes. Our industry-leading resource base of 72 billion oil equivalent barrels includes crude reserves of 22 billion oil equivalent barrels. This resource base provides a diverse source of current producing volumes and future profitable development opportunities.  

The breadth of our portfolio allows us to develop the most attractive projects through a disciplined process of selectivity and efficient deployment of capital. We continued to pursue an unparalleled set of profitable upstream development projects. We have over 70 major projects underway, which will develop 11 billion net oil equivalent barrels of new production. About one-third of our project investments are in North America, while the growth areas of Africa, the Middle East, Russia and The Caspian account for almost 60% of our investments.  

Looking next at the geographic mix of our producing volumes for two points in time, 2003 and the year 2010. You can see, as future development projects bring new resources online, our overall upstream volumes are expected to grow, and the geographical mix of our portfolio is shifting towards ever-greater diversity.  

The established areas of North America, Europe, and elements of Latin America in the Far East are still expected to provide over half of our total volumes by the end of this decade. Significant new resource development projects are underway or planned in the growth areas of Africa, Middle East, Russia and The Caspian.  

Together, these growth areas represented approximately 20% of Exxon Mobil's 2003 volumes. These same growth areas are expected to contribute over 40% of total volumes in the year 2010. Exxon Mobil's global functional upstream organization is designed to manage geographic diversity and the complexities associated with these new emerging areas. It plays to our strengths. Our worldwide experiences over the past century are brought to bear along with our longstanding management in business control systems to ensure that we establish these profitable new operations for the long-term future of success.  

In West Africa, Exxon Mobil has a substantial and profitable production base as well as significant growth potential. Production from this region totaled over 440,000 oil equivalent barrels in 2003 and is expected to double by 2010 to over 900,000 barrels per day net. The Chad/Dover project achieved early oil production in 2003, one year ahead of schedule. Full field startup was in February of this year, also ahead of the plan.  

The project had an exemplary safety record with 40 million hours worked without a lost time incident. In the Chad project, we partnered with the World Bank and the government of Chad to develop an innovative revenue management plan. The plan sits on a process for long-term management of the revenues, whereby all royalties and dividends are dedicated to high-priority poverty relief programs, ensuring the project benefits reach the citizens of Chad.  

In the deepwater areas offshore West Africa, Exxon Mobil holds interest totaling almost 11 million gross acres; 17 deepwater exploration wells were completed in 2003, which added 480 million oil equivalent barrels to the resource base. In Angola, Exxon Mobil has interest in five deepwater blocks that cover 4.5 million acres.  

Together with our co-ventures, we have announced 37 discoveries in Angola to-date with gross total recoverable resource potential of 11.5 billion oil equivalent barrels. Progress on our Angola development project remains on track. Our activities also remained high in Nigeria with a number of offshore development projects underway.  

Major new developments in Russia and The Caspian hold significant growth potential for the company. Production totaled over 100,000 oil equivalent barrels per day net in 2003 with liquid volumes expected to increase more than threefold by the end of this decade. Exxon Mobil holds a 30% interest in and operates Russian Sakhalin-1blocks. In 2003, we commenced an extended-reach drilling program from the largest land-based rig in the world.  

More than 5 billion oil equivalent barrels are expected to be produced from a multiphase Sakhalin-1project. Initial phase will produce 250,000 barrels per day from the Chaivo field with first oil expected late next year. In Azerbaijan, with estimated recoverable resources of over 6 billion barrels of oil and 6 trillion cubic feet of gas at ACG, multiple phases of expansion are planned. Phase I expansion of 400,000 barrels per day to develop the Central Azeri field is on track for a 2005 startup.  

In Kazakhstan, the initial phase development program and budget for the Giant Kashagan field was recently by the government. This world-class field holds an estimated 13 billion barrels of gross recoverable resources.  

The first phase of development will produce 450,000 barrels per day gross with a startup in the year 2008. Also, in Kazakhstan, Exxon Mobil participates in the Tengiz joint venture, where expansions have already increased capacity to 300,000 barrels per day gross.  

Two more expansions are planned for an additional 440,000 barrels per day of gross capacity. The first of these expansions is expected to start up, next year. In addition to these world-class development projects, Exxon Mobil continues to evaluate other opportunities in this resource-rich region.  

In the Middle East, Exxon Mobil continues to progress significant natural gas project to develop Qatar's North field. Gas resources to be developed through existing and planned LNG trains and natural gas projects exceed 22 billion oil equivalent barrels. In February, of 2004, we started up RasGas LNG Train 3, the largest LNG train in the world. This brings the current gross LNG capacity, in which we participate in gutter, to 20 million tons per year with plans to add an additional 41 million tons per year by 2011. These plans include LNG imports projects to Europe and the United States.  

We are making steady progress on developing LNG import terminals for the UK and Continental Europe. In addition, last October, we signed a hedge of agreement with Qatar Petroleum to produce and deliver 15.6 million tons per year of LNG to the United States. This project will be the largest LNG import project in the US. In other areas of the Middle East, our existing oil production is primarily from Abu Dhabi and Yemen. We continue to pursue investment opportunities in Abu Dhabi and Kuwait as well as developing plans for access to other attractive areas in the Middle East, as they arise.  

Large highly profitable and established oil and gas operations in North America, Europe, as well elements of Asia Pacific and Latin America form a strong foundation for our upstream portfolio. In North America, Exxon Mobil maintains the industry's largest portfolios of crude reserves and production. We are pursuing already gas opportunities and advancing LNG import terminals into the US to support the growing need for natural gas. We're also expanding heavy oil and tar sands development in Canada. In Europe, your company is the largest net producer of oil and natural gas. We started seven major offshore developments in 2003, and these projects are expected to provide net daily peak production of 220,000 oil equivalent barrels. We are also advancing a significant number of initiatives, including LNG import terminals and natural gas development projects.  

Exxon Mobil's upstream business is well positioned for the future. We have the industry's largest and highest quality asset base. Our upstream global functional organization yields significant advantages in both cost efficiencies and our ability to respond to an ever-changing business environment. Our upstream business portfolio is underpinned by the corporation's commitment to the development of an application of leading-edge technology. The company's unwavering commitments to business integrity and strict investment discipline are key to achieving long-term sustainable results. All of these efforts are supported by our unmatched financial strength, which allows us to pursue any and all profitable investment opportunities that meet our criteria. When all is said and done, the financial results are the archetypes, which you -- our shareholders -- should and do measure us by. Income per barrel and return on capital employed are what we believe to be the most important metrics of the upstream business. As you can see, on average over the last five years and for last year in particular, we continued to be the leader versus major competitors.  

Now, let's turn to the downstream. Exxon Mobil's refining and supply business manufactures and distributes quality fuels, lubes and other high-value products. We accomplish this through a network of large and highly integrated refineries around the world. Through refining business, scale and integration are important competitive advantages. Overall, our refineries are 80% larger than the industry average, and over 80% of refining capacity is integrated with chemicals or lubes.  

We've demonstrated that our refineries can be operated with industry-leading reliability, which allows us to be more cost and capital efficient. In 2003, we achieved record energy efficiency in our refining operations. We are continuing our longstanding drive to reduce energy consumed at our refineries and pursue energy-efficient cogeneration investments. This effort has added environmental benefits as well.  

As Lee mentioned earlier, molecule management allows us to select the slated crudes for refinery in our network that will provide the highest margin opportunities. We are in the early stages for capturing the financials benefits that, we believe, will come from the full implementation of molecule management technologies. We estimate the potential price to be more than $500 million; and, as best we can tell, no one else in the industry is positioned to replicate this advantage any time soon.  

Our fuels marketing business is comprised of retail, commercial, aviation and marine fuels. We serve motors at nearly 40,000 service stations around the world under three well-recognized brands: Exxon, SO and Mobil.  

We have a portfolio of innovative retail formats designed to appeal the consumers around the world. Many of you have seen our On the Run convenience store format. In the US, our On the Run chain was named the "2003 Convenience Store Chain of the Year." I hope you've had the opportunity before the meeting to enjoy the coffee and the doughnuts at our On the Run coffee bar located outside the lobby. In 2003, we added over 200 new On the Run stores worldwide, bringing the total to 1,000 in 41 countries. Given the intensely competitive nature of the retail business, we must be very selective in our investments.  

We prioritize potential markets globally for investments through a rigorous and disciplined process. We also have a slate of industry-leading loyalty programs, including Speedpass and Upromise. Our research shows that the combined effects of these and other customer loyalty programs can increase our share of an average US household's monthly motor fuel purchases from 10% to nearly 90%.  

We're the world's largest basestock producer and a leading finished lubricants manufacturer. We also have scale advantage in this business. Our average per site basestock manufacturing capacity is over twice the industry average.  

We have built three strong brands with brand equity in each that has been built up over the decades. Exxon Mobil continued to grow its share of the highly profitable synthetic lubricants market in 2003. Mobil 1, the world's first fully synthetic motor oil, originally developed 30 years ago, continues to be the world's top selling synthetic motor oil with double-digit annual sales growth rates. Mobil 1's market position is unparalleled.  

Automobile manufacturers around the world put their trust in Mobil 1, which now boasts factory fuels original equipment status in such high performance automobiles, as Porsche, Mercedes Benz, Aston Martin, Bentley and Cadillac. Beginning in 2003, Mobil branded lubricants were named official lubricants of NASCAR. This association with one of America's fastest-growing supporting events reinforces the Mobil brand's high performance reputation.  

Our overall lubes' offering is well balanced with strong positions in all major customer segments and geographies, and our technical capability is second to none.  

Looking at how the downstream business compares with our major competitors from the year of the merger and this past year. Since the merger, we have maintained the amount of capital employed in the downstream even allowing for roughly $3 billion of investments we've made to meet changing fuel specifications.  

We believe that the selective disciplined capital investments investing at about our rate of depreciation is prudent in this business.  

In contrast, our major competitors have increased their downstream capital base largely through new investments and some acquisitions. If we then look at the earnings being generated from the capital base, you'll see the effect of our relentless attention to cost management and revenue enhancement efforts relative to competition.  

The result of return on capital employed demonstrates the dramatic change in our competitive position over this time period from 1999 to 2003. The improvement in return on capital employed, which we believe is the most crucial measure of performance, underscores our belief that success in the downstream requires sustained commitment to the fundamentals of capital discipline, rigorous cost management, technology leadership, and continuous improvement in all aspects of our business.  

In chemicals, our 2003 sales of 26.6 million tons were equivalent to the record of 2002. Our industry-leading financial performances is closely linked to our unique mix of product lines, advantaged manufacturing assets, and marketing presence. All of our 13 major product lines are managed globally, and 11 of them are ranked either number one or number two in their markets.  

Our exceptional business-mix of commodity, petrochemical products, and less cyclical specialty product lines enhance earnings stability and provide a competitive advantage. More than 90% of our owned and operated chemical capacity is integrated with our large refining complexes or advantaged upstream gas resources. This integration allows us to maximize synergies via optimized molecule management, coordinated technology development, joint facilities planning, and support services.  

In chemicals, as is true across the corporation, our commitment to technology leadership is another key to our success; technology is a major source of differentiation and competitive advantage.  

Chemicals' return on capital employed reached 10.2% in 2003, up from 6.1% in the prior year. This represented our best performance, since 1999. We continued to consistently outperform the competition in return on capital employed. We have demonstrated our leadership throughout the business cycle.  

Thanks to our unique portfolio of businesses. Our new assets in the Middle East and Asia are well positioned to meet Asian demand. Our disciplined focus on improving operational efficiency and other self-helped initiatives are delivering savings to the bottom line.  

We are in a position of strength to be able to take full advantage of the inevitable upturn in the chemical business cycle.  

In our view, the best measure of performance for our capital intensive industry is return on capital employed.  

The facts are that an industry-leading return on capital employed demonstrates the overall ability of the company to not only generate income but to do so on a highly efficient capital base. Your company has outperformed the competition on return on capital employed in any price environment, and this distinguishes us from the competition.  

In summary, I think, you'll agree that, while there are obvious differences across each of our businesses, our approach is remarkably consistent. Your company and its employees remain committed to Exxon Mobil's longstanding core principals that have provided industry-leading results and built strong shareholder value - investment selectivity and discipline, operational excellence, commitment to technology, and enhance to the high standards of safety health, environmental care, and corporate citizenship. These are the core principles that have made us successful in the past, and I have every confidence that they will continue to position us to meet the future challenges. Thank you.

title: ExxonMobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: LEE RAYMOND
speaker: Exxon
text:
Now, I would like to turn to the formal business of the meeting. To begin with, let me make a few brief remarks on shareholder proposals and voting. Each year, the corporation receives a number of suggestions from shareholders. Some of these are in the form of proposals to be presented at the annual meeting, and each is given careful consideration. Typically, we seek a dialogue with the sponsors prior to the meeting, when there is more time to better understand each other's positions and often sign agreements.  

Also, let me be clear on the conduct of the meeting. Recognizing that the majority of our shareholders have voted by proxy and are not present, we have established several procedures to facilitate an orderly meeting. We have setup a process for speakers to identify themselves and quickly get to the microphone to express their views. It is our intent to provide an equal opportunity to speak for all of our shareholders, present today, by allowing speakers on both sides of the issues equal access to the microphone. We ask you to respect this and make your comments from the appropriate microphone.  

In order that as many shareholders as possible can participate, we have set time limits that will be strictly enforced in the time and a system of reminders to help the speakers manage their own time. We have 11 items to consider; as Secretary Mulva said earlier, the discussion period for each item will be limited. This will enable us to have some time for general comments and questions and conclude the meeting in a reasonable timeframe.  

The first item of business is the election of eleven directors. I nominate 11 persons identified on pages 7 through 10 of the proxy statement. These 11 people are highly qualified to continue serving on the board and they're all here today.  

Now I'll ask the nominees who are present and seated to my right in the (inaudible), to stand as their names are called and then I will close the nominations. I have already introduced Rex Tillerson seated here, introduced to you earlier. Michael Boskin, James Houghton, W. R. Howell, Reatha Clark King, Phil Lippincott, Harry Longwell, Henk McKinnell, Marilyn Carlson Nelson and Walter Shipley. Both Don Fites and Helene Kaplan reached mandatory retirement age and retired from the board today after serving on the boards of Mobil and Exxon Mobil since 1990 and 1989 respectively.  

The board and shareholders thank them for their dedicated service to the corporation and wish them well on their retirement. Is there any discussion? Number one.

title: ExxonMobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: ANDREW LOGAN

text:

Good morning. I'd like to cover several aspects of today's meeting. First as we typically note at the outset of similar meetings, estimates, plans and projects discussed today by Mr. Tillerson are forward-looking statements. Actual results, including resource recoveries, volume growth, capital expenditures and project outcomes could differ materially due to factors discussed and those noted under the caption Factors Affecting Future Results on the investor information section of our website.   

I also refer you to the frequently used terms posted on our website, which include definitions of some of the key financial and operating measures we will use today, and additional information required by SEC Regulation G. Before we continue today, I'd like to take this opportunity to familiarize everyone with he safety features of this auditorium. In case of an emergency, we will be notified through the public address system.   

Emergency exits for the ground level as shown on the screen above me are situated at the rear of the auditorium, where you entered and down in front on either side. If we need to evacuate, just proceed to the nearest exit and the Meyerson personnel will guide you to the best way out. In addition, for safety reasons, please do not stand in the aisles or at the back of the hall and do not block the exits.   

To ensure that the meeting is conducted in the interests of all shareholders, there are certain rules of conduct governing this meeting. These rules are posted on signs at the entrances to this meeting, are included in the program and are shown on the screen above me. Let me cover several of the rules.   

The distribution of pamphlets and other literature, banners, signs and other displays is strictly prohibited in this hall. Anyone who intentionally obstructs or interferes with this lawful meeting, by personal action or verbal utterance, is in violation of Texas law. Any persons engaging in such conduct will be asked to cease and if they refuse, they will be escorted from the meeting.   

The laws of New Jersey, where  ExxonMobil is incorporated, provide that no business can be brought up for a vote unless proper notice has been given to all shareholders. Therefore, in fairness to other shareholders not in attendance, and in keeping with the laws that govern our annual meeting, formal business at today's meeting is restricted to the items included in this year's Proxy Statement. Additional proposals may not be introduced from the floor.   

So we can be fair to speakers and other shareholders, please turn off cell phones and pagers at this time if you've not done so already. In order to present a proposal, you must have checked in at the admissions desk in the lobby and verified that you are the proponent or a representative of the proponent, duly authorized under New Jersey law.   

Presenters whose credentials have been verified will be given a blue presenters pass. If neither the proponent nor an authorized representative has checked in and obtained a presenter's pass, we will presume the proponent is not present, and I will move the proposal for the purposes of the orderly conduct of the meeting, and so that shareholder votes may be cast and recorded. However, I will not be acting as representative of the proponent.   

The authorized presenter of a shareholder proposal will have up to three minutes to present the proposal. Time may not be shared with another speaker. No second to the motion is required. Discussion on all items of business will be deferred until the general discussion period later in the meeting.   

Only shareholders as of the record date or their properly appointed proxies are entitled to speak at this annual meeting of  ExxonMobil shareholders. Shareholders making comments during the meeting must speak or have their words translated into English so that the majority of shareholders present can understand what is being said.   

Comments that are offensive or otherwise inappropriate will not be permitted. We would also ask that any issues of personal interest that are not relevant to all shareholders be raised directly with appropriate company representatives outside of the annual meeting. We would request that individual shareholders respect the rights of others to speak and keep their comments as brief as possible.   

If you wish to make comments, you must fill -- first fill out a speaker identification card that is included in the program that was provided to you as you entered the hall. This card confirms that you meet the requirements to speak at this meeting. Give the completed card to the usher when you are recognized to address the meeting.   

To ensure as many shareholders as possible who want to address the meeting today have the opportunity to do so, we ask you to follow these additional instructions. If you would like to address the meeting, move to a reserved aisle seat. Remain seated and raise your hand to indicate to the Chairman that you wish to speak.   

When recognized by the Chairman, give your completed card to the usher and a microphone will be provided. Stand, and begin by stating your name. Unless otherwise provided in these rules, you may speak for up to two minutes. As noted in the Proxy Statement, the Chairman has broad authority to conduct the meeting in an orderly and timely manner.   

Due to the large number of items on today's agenda and the need to conclude the meeting within a reasonable period of time, we cannot assure that every shareholder who wishes to speak will be able to do so. title: Exxon Mobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: REX TILLERSON
speaker: Exxon
text:
Thank you, Henry. Before we move to our items of business, I'd like to spend some time sharing our results with you, and discussing how  ExxonMobil is positioned to meet the world's energy challenges and generate long-term shareholder value.   

Since I spoke with you last year, many things have happened in our industry. In 2006, the price of oil rose to $78, and then fell to $56. Refining margins also increased and then receded, while the chemical industry continued to grow. A number of governments have taken actions to increase their share of the pie in this high priced environment.   

In other words, it was a year for our industry, like many others before it, where geopolitical events and market forces challenged us to capture the maximum value possible for our shareholders under the present conditions, while positioning to deliver future value in the years and decades ahead.   

Let me start with our financial results. By practically every measure, 2006 was an outstanding year. Underpinning these financial results, we again delivered industry leading safety, operational and investment performance, which positioned us to benefit from the robust market conditions.   

Our net income grew to a record $39.5 billion, and return on capital employed was an industry leading 32%. Cash flow from operations and asset sales was $52 billion, allowing distribution to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases of nearly $33 billion, an increase of more than 40% from 2005, and totaling more than $90 billion over the last five years.   

To help put this in perspective, the $90 billion that we've returned to you, our shareholders, is greater than the market value of all the 30 largest US corporations. We also invested $20 billion in the business last year, and continue to identify and progress world-class profitable investment opportunities. Our financial and technical strength allows us to pursue all opportunities that satisfy our rigorous investment criteria.   

Our view of the fundamentals for success in this industry has not changed. It requires consistency, integrity, discipline, reliability and ingenuity.  ExxonMobil has these qualities in abundance and they are applied as part of our robust business model. Hopefully this depiction of our business model is familiar to most if not all of you.   

It begins with investment discipline, focus on long-term fundamentals, the identification of resilient projects, and the delivery of those projects on time and on budget. We apply the same rigor and focus to our operations. We operate to the highest standards, meet our commitments, and in the process set industry benchmarks. We do this through disciplined systematic management processes, we call this operational excellence.   

Throughout the business cycle and across all of our businesses, this approach continues to deliver industry leading returns, superior cash flow and growth and value for you our shareholders. Simply put, the model works. This is a transparent and straightforward approach to doing business that we do not intend to change.   

Let me talk about how we are investing in the future. Our approach to doing investments continues to be shaped by our view of long-term trends in the industry and the global economy. We continue to invest selectively in projects that we believe will be robust across a broad range of industry environments. This discipline to pursue and select the most attractive investment opportunities, I believe, continues to distinguish  ExxonMobil from others.   

In 2006, capital and exploration expenditures were nearly $20 billion or 12% higher than in 2005. The increase reflects some impact from the rising cost environment, but this primarily reflects the progression of additional projects, projects that will add to the value of the company over the coming decades.   

As depicted by the pie diagram on the right, our investments are geographically diverse. Our presence in all regions of the world positions us to pursue and advance all attractive opportunities that meet our criteria. Looking ahead, we have a large inventory of projects underway and others likely to be attractive.   

As a result, we expect to maintain our investment profile in the range of $20 billion per year. While opportunities and actual spending in any given year will likely vary depending on the pace and progress of individual projects, suffice it to say we expect very active levels of investment beyond the end of the decade.   

ExxonMobil is committed to conducting business in a manner that protects the safety, health and security of our employees, our customers and the public, as well as meeting the expectations of our shareholders and the needs of the communities in which we operate.   

To deliver on this commitment, we employ a highly structured management framework, our proprietary Operations Integrity Management System or OIMS. This is used globally to proactively manage risk in our operations. OIMS is effective because the commitment begins with senior management and continues throughout all levels of the organization.   

It is a standard global system embedded into our every day work processes. Now in its 15th year, over time it has become a part of our culture and is second nature to the way our organization works from the top to the bottom. Not only does OIMS enhance safety and environmental performance, it also adds value to the bottom line by improving reliability and lowering our operating costs.   

Nothing receives more management attention than the safety and health of our employees, contractors, customers and the people who live and work in the areas we operate. Worker safety has improved dramatically since the inception of OIMS. The results shown on the chart are equivalent to fewer than five lost time accidents per year per 10,000 workers. Safety is of paramount importance in its own right, but it is also a leading indicator of general operational excellence.   

Discipline, commitment and the effective day-to-day management of the business are factors that lead to excellence in safety performance. These are the same factors that lead to excellence in our operational and our financial performance. As with other elements important to our business success, we are systematic, proactive and globally aligned in our approach to safety.   

Economic and environmental performance in the communities in which we operate is fundamental to our long-term sustainable success. The Operations Integrity Management System is also utilized to manage the environmental risks that are unavoidable aspects of our activities. Our environmental actions and objectives are guided by sound scientific assessments, and are managed as an integral part of our ongoing business.   

Integration into the day-to-day decisions and management of operational activities is key to our progress, and we have been recognized as an industry leader for this approach. Our operational focus areas include reducing hydrocarbon spills, improving energy efficiency and reducing flaring. Our programs and processes are designed and implemented to protect tomorrow today.   

We continue to prudently invest in technology. In 2006, we spent more than $700 million and invested more than $3 billion since 2002, consistently at levels above our competitors. This consistent level of investment demonstrates our commitment to invest in technology development for the long term.   

To maximize the value of our technology efforts, we integrate them into the business planning cycle, and progress is [started] and managed similar to other investments. We balance our research between technology extensions, which can be quickly implemented in our existing operations, and technology breakthroughs that can have a significant and lasting impact on the corporation and the industry as a whole.   

Technology is fundamental to our business. I hope you're able to visit our displays in the entrance lobby, which demonstrate our progress through technology. Our focus on proprietary research delivers competitive advantage. It opens doors to resource opportunities through cost effective solutions in challenging environments. It enables the development of innovative products and new and improved manufacturing processes in the downstream and chemical businesses.   

Maximizing the value from our assets and increasing our competitive advantage is achieved through sustainable business improvement. We continued our superior performance with a five-year average return on capital employed of 24%. And the gap with the competition has continued to grow.   

Our 2006 ROCE of 32% was 50% higher than our competitors. The return on capital employed is a key measure of financial performance for  ExxonMobil, given the long term and capital intensive nature of our industry. Our industry-leading ROCE is a reflection of our portfolio of quality and our underlying capital decision making and operational excellence. This continued focus on long-term values has and will continue to benefit our shareholders.   

I'd now like to move on to the specific performance of our upstream, downstream and chemical businesses, starting with the upstream. The upstream had a record year of earnings in 2006 at just over $26 billion, driven by strong oil and gas prices and we widened the gap with competition by recording a 45.3% return on capital employed.   

Annual average production was 4.2 million oil equivalent barrels per day, an increase of 4% from 2005. We also had another strong year of additions to our total resource base and to our proved reserves. Our upstream capital spending was $16.2 billion, an increase of $1.8 billion versus 2005, reflecting higher levels of drilling and project activity as well as some market factors.   

Underpinning our upstream business is an industry leading reserves base. Shown on the left of this chart is our 2006 year-end proved reserve base, with puts for oil and gas, geographic location and resource type. By any measure, this is a large highly diversified reserve base.   

Our proved reserve replacement trend is shown on the graph to the right. In 2006, we added 2 billion barrels while producing 1.6 billion barrel oil equivalent, yielding a 122% replacement rate. This extends our performance of greater than 100% reserve replacement to 13 consecutive years.   

ExxonMobil's ability to identify and deliver integrated upstream, downstream and chemical concepts to a resource owner can be an important distinction in maximizing resource value, and has been one factor behind our long-term success at growing the reserve base.   

This slide shows examples of the value chain building blocks for gas or crude. Many companies can build these blocks individually.  ExxonMobil has the technology, experience and best-in-class project and operational skills to offer all of these opportunities in any combination as an integrated package.   

It's not just about cost savings generated through economies of scale, energy optimization or shared uses of resources. It's about finding and delivering integrated concepts that squeeze the most value from each hydrocarbon molecule.   

An example is the concept underpinning the agreement with  Qatar Petroleum for a world scale petrochemical complex that utilizes feedstock from  Qatar Petroleum and  ExxonMobil gas developments in the north field, to supply competitively advantaged products to Asia and Europe. The base project will utilize our proprietary steam cracking furnace and polyethylene technologies.   

Upstream, downstream integration that delivers more value for the resource holder is an  ExxonMobil strength, and positions us to capture growth opportunities. We can see the benefits of our integrated approach and excellence in project execution on the next slide with our recent and upcoming startups.   

In 2006, seven major projects began production. They are expected to contribute significant volumes over the coming years, as shown in the graphic to the lower right. The Erha and Erha North Development in Nigeria came on stream and quickly ramped up to over 200,000 barrels a day of oil production. Also in Nigeria, the East Area additional oil recovery project began operations. This project will deliver an incremental 560 million barrels of oil equivalent, and will reduce routine flaring substantially.   

Other startups in 2006 included Dalia in Angola, the Guntong hub offshore peninsula in Malaysia, ACG Phase II in the Caspian, Fram East offshore Norway and a Syncrude upgrader expansion in Canada. We expect seven major developments to come on stream this year that will add nearly 200,000 oil equivalent barrels a day net at peak to our base volumes.   

The expected 2007 startups are located in the North Sea, Qatar and Angola. These projects and startups in 2008 and beyond, combined with work at our existing fields, drives a positive outlook for profitable capacity growth in the future.   

Based on our current expectations, we see continued growth in capacity. While the Americas and Europe are expected to decline slightly, growth is expected as a result of our activities in the Asia-Pacific and Middle East regions, and is supported by continued modest growth on an already sizable base in Africa. Oil is expected to account for about 60% of our annual capacity for the foreseeable future, growth in gas -- in the gas segment will be driven by our major LNG projects in Qatar.   

Each year we update our estimates on project timing, given technical, regulatory and commercial readiness of the projects in our inventory. The capacity outlook shown is the result of that process, and the actual volumes produced might well take a less smooth path due to variables such as weather, geopolitics, regulatory changes and oil price. Our disciplined approach to managing our upstream business is evidenced by the financial results.   

Throughout the price cycle, we have consistently delivered superior performance. That performance is illustrated on this chart.  ExxonMobil's income is growing faster than the competition's, and we are maintaining our capital discipline. As a result, it's no surprise then that our return on average capital employed, perhaps the single best indicator of company performance in this capital intensive long-term business, continues to lead the competition. In 2006, our upstream return on average capital employed of 45% was 80% higher than the competitor's average.   

I'll now turn to our downstream business. In the downstream, we also have record financial performance in 2006, with earnings of $8.5 billion, generating our best ever return on capital employed of 36%. We capitalized on the industry environment with continued strong refinery performance, with throughput of 5.6 million barrels per day, and petroleum product sales of 7.2 million barrels per day.   

These results were underpinned by continued operational excellence. Our safety, environmental performance and energy efficiency were all equivalent to or better than our 2005 record performance. We again delivered over $1 billion of after-tax self-help, through margin enhancements and operating cost efficiencies. We have maintained our disciplined approach to capital management, with downstream capital employed flat since the merger, to our growing capacity to meet demand.   

Many have asked, why we don't build new refineries in mature markets. The answer is really quite simple. We can more efficiently add refining capacity at a level consistent with demand growth at our existing facilities. The top chart illustrates that our global refining distillation capacity has grown about 50,000 barrels per day per year over the last decade.   

Similarly, the bottom chart shows that our global conversion capacity has grown about 35,000 barrels per day per year over this same period. These growth rates are equivalent to building a new refinery every three years, but at obviously at a small fraction of the cost of a new build. Consequently this capacity growth remains economic and resilient over a wide range of industry margin scenarios.   

The situation is different, however, in the less mature markets where more significant investments are needed to meet growing demand. For example, we recently announced, along with our Saudi and Chinese partners, the signing of contracts for the fully integrated refining, petrochemicals and fuels marketing joint venture projects in China.   

This marks a significant milestone in the development of China's first fully integrated project with foreign participation. Plans include an expansion of an existing 80,000 barrel per day refinery, to 240,000 barrels per day. In addition, the project will construct a new 800,000 ton per year steam cracker, with associated polyolefins unit and an aromatics complex.   

There will also be a paired fuels marketing joint venture, which will include approximately 750 retail stations. Integration, leading edge technology, world class operations and participation across the full value chain will ensure competitive advantage in the growing China market.   

This chart illustrates how we have differentiated ourselves in the downstream. The top left shows the results of our capital discipline. We have maintained a flat, in fact slightly lower, capital base over the past five years, despite the significant investments required to meet mandated new product specifications and industry cost pressures.   

In contrast, key competitors have increased their capital employed, largely through new investments and some acquisitions during the same period. The top right illustrates the results of our self-help improvements.   

The bars represent reported earnings, and as you can see we are generating higher earnings than either of our key competitors even with a flat capital base. The chart below summarizes the bottom line ROCE results. Our downstream approach is delivering consistently superior returns for  ExxonMobil shareholders.   

Moving now to the chemical business, which also had an outstanding year. Earnings of $4.4 billion topped the prior year's record of $3.9 billion, and represents the highest in our history. Return on capital employed of 33% was the highest since 1995, and the third consecutive year of performance above 20%, and significantly higher than any of our traditional competitors.   

These results were underpinned by continued operational excellence, including best ever results in employee and contractor safety, as well as energy efficiency and continued delivery of over $450 million of after-tax self-help improvement.   

At the same time, we made significant progress in positioning the company for long-term growth, advancing plans for several world scale advantaged projects to supply increased demand in Asia, in particular China, and further expand our profitable specialties business.   

Over the next ten years, we expect some 60% of the world's petrochemicals growth will occur in Asia, over one-third in China alone. By the year 2015, we expect Asia will account for 50% of global demand for key commodity products, and China alone will represent 25%.   

We have a large existing advantaged asset base in the Middle East and Asia that is ideally positioned to serve these growing markets. These investments are based on long-term competitive advantage, including integration with other operations, advantaged feedstocks and market access.   

In addition, we are pursuing major projects in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Singapore and China to provide additional advantage capacity, to profitably meet future demand in this region. Each project has unique characteristics and is in a different phase of development. Based on these overall plans, we would anticipate increasing our capacity in Asia and the Middle East by more than 50% over the next several years.   

In contrast, our traditional competitors tend to start from a smaller base and have lower announced growth plans. So we are targeting not just to maintain, but in fact grow our lead over competition in these key markets.   

Our returns in our chemical business also differentiate  ExxonMobil from the competition. With respect to capital employed, the major oil competitors have maintained a relatively flat capital base over the past five years. However, earnings of the major oil competitors have remained essentially flat, while ours have grown over five-fold, aided by the pace and magnitude of our self-help improvements.   

Our most comparable chemical-only competitor has increased earnings, but to a lower relative level and from a much higher capital base. Consequently, we are clearly leading key competitors with a 2006 return on capital employed of 33% versus a competitor average of 14%.   

This has been true for the entire business cycle. Over the past ten years we have averaged 16% return on capital employed, compared to estimates of 7% for our traditional oil competitors, and 11% for our most comparable chemical-only competitor.   

In summary, industry-leading performance across our businesses and the business cycle, demonstrates our company's strengths and the rigorous execution of our business model. We have developed a high-performing portfolio of assets that provides advantages in scale, geographic diversity and business mix.   

This portfolio brings balance to overall risks that arise from changes in commodity price, business cycles and local or regional market conditions, while maximizing the long-term value. Our 2006 upstream earnings were the largest in private industry. Downstream profitability continued to grow, and the chemical business outperformed the competition.   

Returning cash to you, our shareholders, in a consistent way has always been a hallmark of  ExxonMobil through our long history of paying dividends. The company has paid a dividend each year for more than century, and has paid out $34 billion in cash dividends to our shareholders over the past five years.   

During this period, we have increased per share dividends to nearly 40% as compared to an increase of 24% for all companies on the S&P 500. We continue to evaluate and manage our dividend policy with a view to building long-term shareholder value and maintaining sufficient financial strength and flexibility to pursue all attractive opportunities that may present themselves.   

In addition to cash dividends, we distribute cash to shareholders through our treasury share purchase program, while maintaining financial flexibility. We proactively work to manage the amount of cash on our balance sheet and our overall capital structure. Annual share purchases increased from $4 billion in 2002, to $25 billion in 2006.   

This represents a six-fold increase in four years and a cumulative distribution to shareholders through share purchases of $58 billion during the period. These purchases have reduced shares outstanding by 16% since the beginning of 2002, or by 12% if one compares average shares outstanding in 2002, with average shares outstanding in 2006.   

Investors often ask how they benefit from these share repurchases. The reduction in shares outstanding increases the ownership interest of the remaining shares. Each remaining share owns more of the company, owns more of the production, more of the reserves, more of the refining throughput and more of the chemical sales.   

As shown on this chart, the growth in per share measures of these key operating metrics has been strong. While production on an absolute basis has been relatively stable over the period, each share now has an interest in 14% more of  ExxonMobil's industry leading production portfolio than in 2002, and 19% more of  ExxonMobil's crude reserves.   

Each share owns 17% more of our refining throughput and our chemical prime product sales. Through this increase in ownership in these key areas, share purchases over the last five years also contributed $0.88 to our 2006 earnings per share.   

As I've highlighted, financial and operational results for 2006 were outstanding and the market rewarded our shareholders with industry-leading returns. However, the financial results and stock market returns for any given year are not the best, or the only indicator to evaluate an industry like ours with multi-decade time horizons. That's why it is useful to examine performance over longer periods of time.   

As you can see, we've generated greater shareholder value than our industry competition, and greater value than the broader market over the last 20 year, ten year and five-year periods. Even more impressive than the fact that we outperformed the competitor average is that  ExxonMobil was the top performer in the competitor group during each of these periods.   

This difference has grown since the merger. And as you can see, with the five-year annual return being 1.4 times greater than the competitor group, and 2.7 times greater than the S&P 500. As we look to the future, we as an organization remain committed to enhancing this competitive advantage.   

Now that concludes my review of the business results. But I'd like now to share a short video with you that speaks to  ExxonMobil's support of math and science education. To ensure continued advancements in technology and innovation, we must have new generations trained in science and math. And we're committed to supporting education initiatives to encourage and develop young people in this critical area.   

(VIDEO PLAYS AND RESUMPTION OF SESSION)   

Now, I'd like to turn to the formal business of the meeting. To begin, let me make a brief remark on shareholder proposals and voting. Each year the corporation receives a number of suggestions from shareholders. Some of these are in the form of proposals to be presented at the annual meeting, and each is given careful consideration.   

Typically we seek a dialogue with the proponents and the sponsors prior to the meeting when there is more time to better understand each other's position. And often we find agreement. Let me be clear on the conduct of the meeting. Recognizing that the majority of our shareholders have already voted by proxy and are not present, we have established procedures to facilitate an orderly meeting.   

We've set up a process for speakers to identify themselves and to express their views, and we welcome those views. In order that as many shareholders as possible can participate, we have set time limits and a system of reminders to help speakers manage their time.   

We have 17 items to consider. As Secretary Hubble said earlier, discussion on all items of business will be deferred to the general discussion period. This will enable us to have some time for general comments and questions, as well as to conclude the meeting in a reasonable time frame.   

We recognize that the meeting may last for several hours, and for those of you who wish to leave the meeting at any time, I do want to express to you my appreciation for your attendance. Since we have a number of items yet to discuss on the program, I'd invite any of you, if you you'd like to take about a 30 second stretch break -- just stand up, stretch your legs, and then I'll call you back to order. I ask that you do not leave the hall.

All of our nominees currently serve as  ExxonMobil Directors except for Mr. Steven Reinemund, who has been nominated by the Board for first election as a director at this meeting. The recommendation of Mr. Reinemund as a candidate was developed by the incumbent, non-employed Directors of the Board Affairs Committee.

Can we have some lights? Thank you. William George. James Houghton. William Howell. Reatha Clark King. Philip Lippincott. Marilyn Carlson Nelson. Sam Palmisano. Steven Reinemund. Walter Shipley. Steve Simon.   

I'm pleased to note that we have 100% of our Directors in attendance at this shareholder meeting, which has been a tradition for some time. I declare the polls open for all who want to vote in the election of the Directors and the 16 remaining items.   

If you wish to change your proxy instructions on the elections of Directors or any of the other 16 items, or if you have not submitted a proxy and wish to vote by ballot, they are available from the ushers. Please raise your hand if you would like a ballot and at any time during the formal business. They will be collected after all items have been discussed.   

The next item on the agenda is the ratification of  PricewaterhouseCoopers as independent auditors. The Audit Committee of the Board has appointed  PricewaterhouseCoopers to audit  ExxonMobil's financial statements for 2007, and we are asking shareholders to ratify that appointment.  PricewaterhouseCoopers is represented here by Mr. Jonathan Mullins.   

The Audit Committee's reasons for recommending  PricewaterhouseCoopers appear in the Proxy Statement. I move the adoption of the proposal as shown on pages 44 and 45 of the Proxy Statement. The next order of business is consideration of the 15 shareholder proposals in the Proxy Statement.

title: Exxon Mobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: ROBERT MONKS
speaker: Investor
text:
Mr. Tillerson, the annual meeting of  ExxonMobil is a very important occasion. It is pleasant that in addition to the usual shareholders, the nuns, the priests and the monks, you also have today representatives of some of the great long-term shareholders of America.   

I'd like to make known that the State Treasurer of the State of Connecticut, Denise Nappier, the Assistant Treasurer, Meredith Miller and the Controller of the State of California, John Chung, are here. And they are the kind of shareholders who are long-term shareholders. And from the point of view of being interested shareholders, they are probably the leading element in America today.   

And I hope because this resolution on cumulative voting has to do essentially with the problem of, who does the Board work for? Does the Board work for the management, or does it work for the shareholders? I hope you will take advantage of having these major shareholders here, and will make some kind of effort to talk with them and to find out what's on their minds.   

Now, with the presentation you've given, Mr. Chairman, and I want to applaud you on it. And I particularly want to applaud in my own life what a joy it is to be an Exxon shareholder, and to contemplate the safety record you have with your American refineries. That must be a pleasure for everyone associated with Exxon.   

Now there are certain questions, where the shareholders really do need to be heard. The kinds of questions are, how did this company respond to the letter from Senator Rockefeller and Senator Snowe? I don't know Mr. Tillerson, whether you personally talked with them. I don't know Mr. Tillerson, whether any one of the Board Committees talked with them.   

But I do know that when a United States senator, or two United States senators who are moderate people make a statement about  ExxonMobil having a derogatory role in the world, about America's presence, that that needs to be answered. As a shareholder, I want to know how it was answered. At the moment, I have to say that this resolution for allowing cumulative voting would permit shareholder representation on the Board. And for certain of these issues we need it.   

Let me assure you that cumulative voting is not a way of opening the gate, and having utterly unmotivated people be present. All this resolution says is that a given percentage of the shareholders can assure that someone's on the ballot. But that's when the fun begins. They have to get their own ballot cards, they have to get their own shareholder lists, they have to circulate that.   

And let me tell you, anybody who's willing to do that, is a serious enough person that they ought to be considered for membership on the Exxon Board. They also have to get more votes than the other nominees. So I would suggest, Mr. Chairman, that cumulative voting is a good idea, and I would hope that the management in future years would initiate it. Thank you.

Thank you, very much. Good morning, Mr. Tillerson. Good morning members of the Board. And I thank you very much for your time today, to fellow shareholders. My name is Patricia Daley and I'm a Dominican Sister of Caldwell New Jersey, and I'll be presenting a shareholder resolution later on, but Mr. Steiner asked me to move this resolution today.   

I've been here at meetings at  ExxonMobil for probably ten years or more, and actually at least consistently, and have been in this gathering since the '80s, I believe. I'm part of the Interface Center on Corporate Responsibility, which is an organization of 275 Jewish, Roman Catholic and Protestant institutional investors.   

We hold about $120 billion worth of investment power, and today our membership also includes the healthcare systems, foundations, unions, investment managers, foundations. So, a number of institutional investors who rely on the returns, great returns that we see here from our company.   

Institutional investors who not only rely on fiscal return, but believe that the social and ecological concerns that those elements are integrally important and very connected to the fiscal health of any company in the industry.   

125 years ago, our company was incorporated in the State of New Jersey and just as a little background, in order to receive a certificate of incorporation for any company, any publicly owned company or any company, you don't -- you need to be able to state that you're in business for more than just making money.   

Companies have an obligation to contribute to the common good in society. That's part of what the responsibility is and part of the responsibilities of the Board members; to assure shareholders and assure the State of New Jersey that you are -- you continue to be faithful to the incorporation documents.   

Today there are -- there will be people raising questions --I'll be talking about global warming later on. Clearly in the last ten years of our conversations around climate change, we now see it's another whole world, I would say, since even we were here last year. People understand not just the greater concerns around global warming, but also how critical a business issue the impact on the economy would be.   

So with -- today, we're going to hear about some of that. We're going to hear about the connections between ecological, social and fiscal concerns as corporate governance concerns as well. I thank you for your time, and as a courtesy to Mr. Steiner, move this resolution asking for a special meeting. Thank you.
