title: Exxon Mobil Corporation Shareholders Meeting
name: VP - IR AND CORPORATE SECRETARY
speaker: Exxon
text:
Good morning, I would like to cover several aspects of today's meeting. First, as we typically note at the outset of similar meetings, statements of future events or conditions included in Mr. Tillerson's remarks today are forward-looking statements.

Actual future results, including resource recoveries, volume growth, capital expenditures, project outcomes and the XTO Energy transaction could differ materially due to factors discussed and those noted under the caption "Factors Affecting Future Results" on the Investor section of our website. I also refer you to the frequently used terms posted on our website which include definitions of some of the key financial and operating measures we will use today, and additional important information.

Before we continue today, I would like to take this opportunity to familiarize everyone with the safety features of this auditorium. In case of an emergency, we will be notified through the public address system. Emergency exits for the ground level as shown on the screen above me are situated at the rear of the auditorium, where you entered and down front on either side. If we need to evacuate, just proceed to the nearest exit and the Meyerson personnel will guide you to the best way out. In addition, for safety reasons, please do not stand in the aisles or at the back of the hall, and do not block the exits.

To ensure that the meeting is conducted in the interests of all shareholders, there are certain rules of conduct governing this meeting. These rules are posted on signs at the entrances to the meeting, are included in the program, and are shown on the screen above me.

Let me now cover several of the rules. The distribution of pamphlets and other literature, banners, signs and other displays is strictly prohibited in the hall. Anyone who intentionally obstructs or interferes with this lawful meeting by physical action or verbal utterance is in violation of Texas law. Any persons engaging in such conduct will be asked to cease, and if they refuse they will be escorted from the meeting.

The laws of New Jersey, where ExxonMobil  is incorporated provide that no business can be brought up for a vote unless proper notice has been given to all shareholders. Therefore, in fairness to other shareholders not in attendance, and in keeping with the laws that govern our annual meeting, formal business at today's meeting is restricted to the items included in this year's proxy statement. Additional proposals may not be introduced from the floor.

So, we can be fair to all speakers and other shareholders, please turn off all cell phones and pagers.

In order to present a proposal, you must have checked in at the admissions desk in the lobby and verified that you are the proponent or representative of the proponent, duly authorized under New Jersey law.

Presenters whose credentials have been verified will be given a blue presenter's pass. If neither the proponent nor an authorized representative has checked in and obtained a presenter's pass, we will presume the proponent is not present and I will move the proposal for the purposes of the orderly conduct of the meeting and so that the shareholder votes cast may be recorded. However, I will not be acting as a representative of the proponent.

The authorized presenter of the shareholder proposal will have up to three minutes to present the proposal. Time may not be shared with another speaker and no second to the motion is required. Discussion on all items of business will be deferred until the discussion period later in the meeting.

Only shareholders as of the record date, or their properly opponent -- appointed proxies are entitled to speak at this annual meeting of ExxonMobil  shareholders. Shareholders making comments during the meeting must speak, or have their words translated into English so that the majority of shareholders present can understand what is being said. Comments that are offensive or otherwise inappropriate will not be permitted.

We would ask that any issues of personal interest that are not relevant to all shareholders be raised directly with appropriate company representatives outside of the annual meeting. We request that individual shareholders respect the rights of others to speak and keep their comments as brief as possible. As noted in the proxy statement, the chairman has broad authority to conduct the meeting in an orderly and timely manner.

If you wish to make comments, you must first fill out a speaker identification card that is included in the program that was provided to you as you entered the lobby. This card confirms you meet the requirements to speak at this meeting. Give the completed card to the usher when you are recognized to address the meeting.

To ensure as many shareholders as possible who want to address the meeting today have the opportunity to do so, we ask you to follow these additional instructions. If you would like to address the meeting, move to a reserved aisle seat, remain seated and raise your hand, holding your speaker identification card to indicate to the chairman that you wish to speak. When recognized by the chairman, give your completed speaker card to the usher and a microphone will be provided. Stand, and begin by stating your name. Unless otherwise provided in these rules, you may speak for up to two minutes.

Due to the large number of items on today's agenda, and the need to conclude the meeting within a reasonable period of time, we cannot assure that every shareholder who wishes to speak will be able to do so. First priority will be given to those who have not yet had an opportunity to speak.

As we have done in the past, we have provided a timing system with lights that will help speakers manage their time. I would like to demonstrate the system at this time. When the chairman recognizes a speaker and a microphone has been provided by the usher, a green light will come on at the displays on both sides of the stage. The hall microphones will be activated only after the speaker has been recognized by the chairman. When the speaker's time remaining reaches 30 seconds, a yellow light will turn on. A red light will indicate the speaker is at the end of the time allowed. Thank you.

REX TILLERSON : Thank you, David. Shortly, we will address our items of business, however, I'd first like to share with you some highlights from our 2009 results. As most of you will recall, 2008 was a record year for our company and our industry. However, in 2009 the business environment was dramatically different.

In spite of the challenging business environment, ExxonMobil 's businesses delivered strong performance in all segments. We remain focused on our business plan, a robust exploration program, record capital investment, and a relentless focus on operational excellence. Our business model, our disciplined approach, and our dedication to rigorous long term planning continue to distinguish ExxonMobil .

Overall, I'm pleased with our 2009 performance. We delivered strong results in a period of significant market challenges. Our safety performance, excellence in operations and superior financial results once again led our industry. Earnings of $19.3 billion and return on average capital employed of 16% were strong despite the significant drop in commodity prices and the impact of the global recession on demand for many of our products.

Cash flow from operations and asset sales was $30 billion. This allowed for distributions to shareholders through dividends and share purchases of $26 billion. We continued our robust, disciplined investment program in 2009, investing a record $27 billion into our business. Our financial strength, and technical and operational expertise allow us to invest through the business cycle, positioning us for the long term.

In 2009, we again added more reserves than we produced. This marks the 16th consecutive year our reserve replacement rate has exceeded 100%. Following the global financial crisis, total shareholder return was a negative 12.6%, reversing the strong relative performance in 2008. While a single year result is never a good way to measure long-term performance, I am nonetheless not happy about a negative shareholder return.

However, I am satisfied that our financial performance allows us to continue to invest for the future, and position ourselves to capitalize on the opportunities on offer in the current business environment. These results are a tribute to the hard work, diligence and focus of the more than 80,000 men and women who work on ExxonMobil 's behalf.

Now, I'd like to review our safety performance as an important indicator of how well our enterprise operates. As many of you have heard me say before, nothing receives more management attention at ExxonMobil  than the safety and health of our employees, our contractors, our customers and the people who live and work in the areas where we operate.

The tragic incident in the Gulf of Mexico, which claimed the lives of 11 industry workers and continues to impact the local environment and economy, reminds us all of the need to be ever vigilant in the area of safety and environmental protection. ExxonMobil  is continuing to provide assistance to BP in responding to the well control incident and the spill, and we are eager to support efforts to determine how much an -- how such an incident can be prevented in the future.

In 2009, our combined employee and contractor workforce achieved a best-ever lost-time incident rates. Our safety performance continued to lead the industry and we are proud of this achievement. Within ExxonMobil , we know that good safety performance leads to good business performance. Our vision that nobody gets hurt is a central element of our daily operational excellence. At ExxonMobil , we pursue excellence in safety performance using a systematic, pro-active and a globally aligned approach.

The people of ExxonMobil  are dedicated to the highest standards of safety and health, and remain committed in maintaining and improving upon these already high levels of performance. To do so requires diligence and innovation. An organization cannot become complacent nor content with past safety performance and we are determined not to be satisfied until we can conclude each day where nobody gets hurt.

Let's now look at our environmental performance. Meeting the world's growing need for energy while managing impacts on the environment is today one of society's grand challenges. Meeting the energy needs of present generations, while protecting the environment for future generations, has to be our collective objective.

At ExxonMobil , we achieve this through rigorous environmental management programs and each business unit has an environmental business plan that delivers consistent, continuous improvement in our global environmental performance. Steps taken since 2005 have reduced our greenhouse gas emissions by more than 9 million metric tons in 2009, which is equivalent to taking 1.9 million cars off of the road in the United States.

One of the most important areas of improvement is energy efficiency. We are on track to meet targets for improving energy efficiency across our worldwide refining and petrochemical operations by at least 10% by the year 2012. We also have specific initiatives to reduce hydrocarbon flaring associated with our operations. In 2009, upstream hydrocarbon flaring was more than 20% lower than in 2008, and was down almost 50% from levels only a few years ago.

Ongoing improvements in reducing spills and releases resulted in zero oil spills from company owned and operated marine vessels in 2009. Flaring and spill performance are just two measures of environmental performance. Additional metrics and details on our performance can be found in our corporate citizenship report which is available at our publication booth in the lobby.

In our current operations and as we develop projects for the future, we will continue working to protect tomorrow today.

Let's now take a look at the 2009 financial results. Again, during a period of challenging industry conditions, as I mentioned, we earned $19.3 billion. These results led the industry. Despite volatile commodity prices, weak refining margins and lower demand for our products, each of our three business segments; upstream, downstream and chemicals achieved industry leading results. These results were achieved while maintaining our steadfast commitment to operations excellence.

Capitalizing on our distinct competitive advantages, including a high quality portfolio of assets that is differentiated from our competition by its scale, geographic diversity and the level of integration throughout our global operations, our consistent commitment to technology and the strength of our global functional organizations, we not only delivered industry leading earnings, but also industry leading returns.

In 2009, ExxonMobil 's return on capital employed was an industry leading 16.3%, more than 50% higher than our nearest competitor, reflecting the strength of our integrated portfolio, and the consistent execution of our business model. We manage each of our business lines for the long term and each of our three business lines also led the competition across all segments. Our commitment to operations excellence is central to the execution of ExxonMobil 's business strategies and creates the foundation to achieve industry leading returns.

The objective of operational excellence is embedded in our company culture, and is fundamental to the way we work every day. Continuing to invest in the business is vital to the long-term success of our company. In 2009, we invested $27 billion back into the business, a record level for ExxonMobil . Over the past five years, we have invested over $110 billion in attractive projects across all business lines.

A disciplined approach to investing through the business cycle with no write downs of assets has established a long record of responsible stewardship of our shareholders' money. We remain committed to advance attractive opportunities that will be robust across a broad range of industry and market conditions while maintaining capital efficiency. These investments reflect the ongoing execution of long term business plans designed to position the business for long term growth and sustainability.

In 2009, we again demonstrated our commitment to reliable and growing dividends for our shareholders through the economic cycle. Over the past five years, we distributed over $38 billion in dividends to shareholders. During this same period, we increased our per share dividends 57%, representing an average growth rate of more than 9% per year compared to the USCPI of about 2.6% annually. Since 1983, through economic cycle ups and downs, shareholders have received annual per share dividend increases.

In addition to growing dividends, we have also provided added flexibility in returns to shareholders via share repurchases. While our major competition discontinued their programs in 2009, we distributed $18 billion to shareholders through share repurchases. On a cumulative basis, distribution to shareholders were $119 billion over the last five years. Purchases have reduced shares outstanding by 26% since the beginning of the year 2005.

We continue to believe the share purchase program is an effective way not only to distribute value to shareholders, but also to increase shareholders' ownership of ExxonMobil 's underlying assets and our operations. The combination of ExxonMobil 's industry-leading business results and share purchase program represent a sustainable approach to increasing shareholder value.

For example, each share of ExxonMobil  has an interest in 26% more production volumes than in 2005. Over the same period, each share now owns 34% more proved reserves, and 22% more refining throughput capacity. Comparing these results to our competition reinforces how beneficial the share purchase program has been to shareholders.

For instance, since 2005, ExxonMobil  has delivered annual oil equivalent production per share growth of 6%, more than 2% higher than our nearest competition. This value is further reflected in the earnings per share. In 2009, earnings per share were $3.98 demonstrating strong business performance, again, under some pretty challenging conditions.

The chart on the left shows the cumulative impact of the share purchase program on earnings per share since the ExxonMobil  merger. Earnings per share in 2009 were 44% higher than would be the case if 2009 earnings had been divided by the number of shares outstanding in the year 2000. Importantly, this impact is ongoing through each economic cycle and is a benefit to all shareholders.

Now, I'd like to share our views on the long term trends that shape ExxonMobil 's business plans. As the world recovers from the economic downturn, and it will, ExxonMobil  will continue to look beyond the current business environment. Our planning horizon is long term, and our view of -- as is our view of energy supply.

Each year, we take a broad in-depth assessment of the global energy marketplace and we publish a comprehensive report entitled, "The Outlook for Energy". The Outlook serves as a foundational document for our business plans. Despite the recent economic downturn, global energy demand, largely driven by developing nations is expected to return, growing with -- an increasing by almost a third over the next 25 years as population growth continues in the developing world. Living standards improve and global economies do expand.

To meet these growing needs and ensure reliable and affordable energy, all economic energy sources will be needed. The bar chart on the left shows demand growth from 2005 to the year 2030 by energy type. In 2005, fossil fuels provided approximately 80% of the world's energy, led by oil, coal and natural gas. Nuclear, hydro-electric, geothermal, biomass along with wind, solar and biofuels make up the remaining 20%.

Now, if we look to the year 2030, the global energy mix remains largely unchanged. Oil still dominates, but natural gas surpasses coal on anticipated very strong growth, particularly as the favored fuel of choice to meet increasing electric power generation needs.

Today, global energy demand -- or total global energy demand in 2030 is expected to rise by about 160 quadrillion BTUs or 1.2% annually, with growth concentrated in non-OECD countries. Importantly, this outlook anticipates that energy efficiency will play an increasingly important role in meeting that future growth in demand.

The bar on the far right shows that the energy saved through projected efficiency gains is expected to be about twice the growth in global energy demand, making energy efficiency vital to meeting future demand needs. This long-term view is the basis for our investment plans.

Energy is the life blood of modern economies. For this reason, we plan to invest more than $125 billion over the next five years, developing future energy supplies, investing in communities in which we operate while reducing the environmental impact of what we do. To meet the dual challenge, meeting energy demand while mitigating impacts on the environment will require a set of integrated solutions.

First, we are expanding commercially viable energy sources to enhance the availability of reliable and affordable energy to consumers the world over. Second, we are accelerating gains in energy efficiency which conserve supplies, reduce the growth rate of greenhouse gas emissions and lower overall energy cost. And third, we are developing and deploying technologies to help mitigate the growth of emissions associated with energy use. We are pursuing each of these three elements vigorously and maintaining our commitment to technology to help meet the global energy challenge.

Now, let's look at each one of these in more detail, starting with expanding supply. In 2009, we started up nine major projects which are forecast to produce almost 400,000 net oil equivalent barrels per day in the year 2010. In partnership with Qatar Petroleum , we began production from the three largest liquefied natural gas trains in the world and commenced send out from two LNG terminals in Europe, all supported by a fleet of the most efficient LNG carriers in the world.

In addition, the Al Khaleej Gas phase two project started up in late 2009, and hedging our position in the growing domestic gas markets in Qatar. At the Piceance Basin in Colorado, we started up phase one development and expect production of 150 million cubic feet per day in 2010. In Europe, we achieved startup of the Tyrihans field offshore Norway.

In China, the highlight of this past year was the startup of our integrated complex in Fujian province. Fujian is China's first fully integrated joint venture, refining the petrochemical complex, combining for the first time in one joint venture; a refinery, petrochemical plant and a retail fuels marketing business.

The new capacity complements our existing facilities in Singapore, and our existing joint ventures in the Middle East. Overall, 2009 was a very significant year for project startups.

Now, let me share a brief review of our portfolio of holdings by resource type. ExxonMobil  has built a significant global liquefied natural gas portfolio. In Qatar, we have developed and applied new technologies to construct the world's largest LNG trains and ships, minimizing unit cost and maximizing the value of the natural gas from Qatar's north field.

ExxonMobil 's share of LNG production in Qatar was just under 39 million tons in 2009. We are actively expanding our project expertise developed for cutter as we progress the Papua New Guinea LNG development along with the Gorgon Jansz LNG development in Australia. These and other projects we're pursuing will result in our participation in about 100 million tons per year of LNG capacity in the coming years.

The unconventional gas business is currently our fastest growing resource type, and we have already accumulated a large, attractive global and conventional gas portfolio. In North America, our acreage position is approximately 700,000 net undeveloped acres. With significant exposure in the Marcellus Shale, the Horn River Basin, the East Texas Haynesville and Eagle Ford Shale in South Texas. In the rest of the world, we have approximately 4.7 million net undeveloped acres, including a broad-based acreage position in Europe and Indonesia.

At the Piceance Basin, our technology leadership in areas such as multi-zone stimulation and fast drill are cost-effectively developing this world-class resource of about 45 trillion cubic feet. These experiences and technologies are well-placed to apply to our growing portfolio of unconventional holdings elsewhere in the world.

In late 2009, ExxonMobil  and XTO Energy announced an all-stock transaction that will enhance ExxonMobil 's position in the development of unconventional natural gas and oil resources. We are confident that the combination of our complementary strengths, both resource holdings and technologies will open new opportunities in these emerging but very important new-energy supplies.

Ongoing technology developments are positioning acid and sour gas resources for future growth. ExxonMobil  has extensive experience in handling and processing of acid-sour gas using subsurface reinjection technology.

At our LaBarge development in Wyoming, carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide are separated from the natural gas and re-injected into the subsurface. Our Controlled Freeze Zone Demonstration Plant in Wyoming will start up in the next month or so and has the potential to provide a cost breakthrough that would allow commercialization of additional high-cost acid and sour gas resources. The technology also has potential application in carbon capture and storage.

In the Arctic, we have an exciting portfolio of oil and gas opportunities. At the Sakhalin Project in Fareast Russia, our technology and project excellence enabled the development of the Chayvo Field resulting in industry-leading performance. New technologies were applied to drill world-record extended-reach wells and design ice-resistant platforms as well as off-loading facilities to enable year-around operations in these very extreme Arctic conditions.

Our experience in Arctic development is positioning us for subsequent development in Sakhalin and for future projects in Alaska and Canada. In addition, we are pursuing new exploration plays in the Canadian Beaufort and off-shore Greenland.

Another growth area is heavy oil and oil sands. Our decades of experience at Cold Lake in Canada in Syncrude provide us with a strong foundation with further phases of development underway at Cold Lake. The Coral Project remains the lowest cost new oil sands project under development in Canada.

We have developed a suite of proprietary technologies that allows to develop these resources at the lowest unit cost in industry including our bitumen treating process called High Temperature Paraffinic Froth Treatment which illuminates the need for a costly up-grader greatly reducing the upfront capital investment.

We continue to hold a strong deepwater position where we have best-in-class performance from our producing assets. In addition, we have a significant portfolio of development projects, and we are actively exploring to add more to this portfolio.

Our industry-leading project execution capabilities coupled with our broad experience in all deepwater technologies ensure we maximize the value of these opportunities. We're also focused on break-through technologies in areas such as hydrate mitigation to extend our abilities to develop these opportunities more cost effectively in the future.

And finally, the high quality of our conventional portfolio continues to provide a strong foundation for our overall asset base. It is here that we develop many of the best practices that we continue to successfully leverage around the Gulf -- the globe, and we continue to identify opportunities and efficiencies in these operations to ensure leading life-cycle profitability. We apply a wide array of technologies in these assets, including advance geological modeling with high-resolution seismic to identify new opportunities in our producing fields.

Now, let's talk about efficiency and emissions as solutions to the energy challenges. We recognize the value that improved efficiency can unlock through reduced energy uses and significantly reduce emissions. In our own operations over the past several years, efficiency at our refining and chemical operations has improved at a rate of 2 to 3 times faster than the industry average due in part to our proprietary furnace technology and our Global Energy Management System known as GEMS.

We are also advancing solutions to help consumers reduce their energy use through development of a variety of technologies that are already available today. These include tire liners to keep tires inflated longer, Mobil 1 Advanced Fuel Economy synthetic engine oils and light-weight automotive plastics.

For the mid and longer term, we are working on a number of other game-changing breakthrough technologies that address the need for both improved fuel economy and reduce the emissions. At ExxonMobil , we are taking a proactive approach to managing long-term risk of climate change. Beyond our efforts to help consumers reduce emissions through increased efficiency and technology advancements, we are reducing greenhouse gas emissions in our own operations and researching and developing breakthrough technologies.

Since 2004, we have invested $1.9 billion in activities that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve our energy efficiency. Additionally, we have invested more than $5 billion in gas utilization and commercialization projects to reduce routine natural gas flaring. We are also expanding our investments in cogeneration, a highly efficient form of energy production to reduce emissions further in our operations.

REX TILLERSON : I'm quite proud of our operational performance, our financial results and our people. As we navigate the global recession and the recovering economy, ExxonMobil  will continue to employ our business model to implement our strategies.

As I mentioned earlier, we lead the industry with our low incident rates for work-related injuries and illnesses, and the system underpins our safety, health, environment and security risk management.

Yes, good morning. My name is Sister Susan Mika. I'm a Benedictine Sister. I live in San Antonio and I'm here today representing the shares of the Needmore Fund which is the primary sponsor of this.

I'm pleased to move the shareholder proposal asking our company to give shareholders a say-on-pay in the form of an advisory vote to ratify the Board compensation report. Needmore sponsored this resolution last year and it received 41.4% of the vote which seems a very strong showing indicating that many of the shareholders desire this reform.

As we're all aware in the room today, the controversy around executive pay has received a new level of intensity in this past year. There's been much press coverage on this issue. There's a bill requiring companies to hold an advisory vote passed by the House of Representatives and it's now in the Senate with high expectations that it will pass.

Our Board Compensation Committees and many of companies are carefully scrutinizing compensation policies and practices as never before, and I know that some of those persons are here with us today. Close to 70 companies have stepped up and agreed to implement this say-on-pay starting either this year or in 2011.

It's been adopted by companies such as Vizor, Intel, Microsoft , ConocoPhillips  and Goldman Sachs  to name a few. And this year the SEC, Securities Exchange Commission, passed formal guidelines for companies taking TARP funds, mandating them to implement an advisory vote.

So in summary to this, it's widely expected that some form of say-on-pay will become standard for companies. We believe that our resolution would institutionalize a formal annual method of communication for investors to give boards feedback on compensation reports and complement other forms of communication with investors.

ExxonMobil  has always been very open in receiving feedback from investors whatever the issue, but all the power on compensation rests with the Board which is free to ignore our input. We seek some checks and balances where investors have an actual vote which is a much stronger message than simply sending a letter to the Board which you answer us.

We believe that the current system of paying CEOs and top management in the US is in serious need of reform. In fact in the US, CEO pay packages average 400 times that of the average employee while in the United Kingdom, it's only 41 times. So, we believe that good governance usually enhances shareholder value by creating accountability to your owners. So, we would urge all shareholders to vote for this proposal. Thank you so much.

My name is Christine Jantz from NorthStar Asset Management in Boston and we are the beneficial owners of 2,209 shares of ExxonMobil  common stock. I'm here today to ask for your support in the creation of a comprehensive Human Right to Water Policy in our company.

In light of the recent British Petroleum  disaster in the Gulf of Mexico, we are all keenly aware of the potential hazardous environmental impact of companies like ours. During this time, the tremendous public awareness about the impact the oil industry could have on water resources and the communities in which we operate, we, as socially responsible investors, want to make sure that ExxonMobil  stays ahead of the curve in terms of our manufacturing effects on water resources.

Human survival is completely dependent on the availability of water, and because of this, there is a substantial global movement of afoot among corporations and nations to recognize the human right to water. This human right has been identified by the United Nations as all people's right to safe, sufficient, accessible, physically accessible and affordable water for personal and domestic use.

In some ways, our company policies touch on aspects of upholding this human right, but they fall far short of creating a comprehensive policy for the Company to use as a guideline in manufacturing and assessing our impact on the communities in which we operate.

Last year, a South African high court declared that the human right to water was guaranteed to all its citizens. France recognizes this right in their National Water Bill and courts in India have recognized this as part of their right to life provision. National constitutions in 10 additional countries have or are developing provisions in their constitutions guaranteeing the human right to water.

In this rapidly changing global economy with several nations already upholding the human right to water, we fear that our company may be subject to costly closer scrutiny simply because we have not outlined for stakeholders, customers and employees exactly what's supporting the human right to water means at ExxonMobil . This is an opportunity for ExxonMobil  to publicly recognize the potential impact it can have upon the residence of local and foreign communities and avow that the health and wellbeing of those residents is a top priority.

As we watch our competitors pour oil into the Gulf of Mexico, it is essential that we take this cue to create an internal policy that will clearly outline our commitment to corporate practices which support every individual's human right to water. This comprehensive policy will protect and maximize our shareholder value. To support the creation of this policy, please vote for resolution number seven.

Good morning. My name is Michael Passoff and I'm here on behalf of Green Century Capital Management to present item number nine, report on Canadian oil sands. This resolution requests that the Board of Directors prepare a report discussing possible long-term risk for the Company's finances and operations posed by the environmental, social and economic challenges associated with oil sand.

Canada's oil sands are the second-largest oil resource in the world comprising of over 173 billion barrels in reserves. Extraction and conversion of oil sands as useful fuel is energy-intensive and environmentally damaging, requiring deforestation, extensive water use and the creation of massive amounts of toxic waste. Even using the most conservative life-cycle analysis, oil from this source submits between 15% and 40% more greenhouse gasses than the average of conventional sources.

Our Company has significantly invested in oil sands through ExxonMobil Canada and through its 70% ownership with Imperial Oil. Nearly 25% of Exxon's liquid reserves and 11% of our Company's total crude reserves are located in oil sand. 88% of Imperial's crude reserves consist of oil sands mining. Investors and independent analysts have raised doubts about the long-term economic viability of oil sands development given the high cost of extraction and converting oil sands along with risk of future profitability presented by the rise in carbon cost and oil price fluctuation.

Local indigenous communities affected by oil sand pollution such as the Beaver Lake Cree Nation have filed legal challenges that can drastically slow or halt the oil sands development. Our Company lags behinds its peers in disclosing these environmental, social and economic risks that it may face because of its presence in the Canadian oil sands.

In the absence of meaningful disclosure, shareholders have no way of knowing how Exxon understands and addresses these significant risks and cannot be assured that our shareholder value is solely protected. We urge you to vote for in support of item number nine; report on Canadian oil sands. Thank you.

Yes. Me again. Good morning, my name is Michael Passoff of As You Sow and I'm here to, on behalf of The Park Foundation, a long-term shareholder that holds approximately 17,000 shares. This proposal asks that the Company report in the environmental impacts of hydraulic fracturing. This proposal is based on two concepts essential to investor confidence -- disclosure and the mitigation of risk.

The merger of XTO Energy will make Exxon the largest natural gas company in the country. It also means that Exxon is now in the center of the storm over hydraulic frac'ing. ExxonMobil  tells us that hydraulic frac'ing is perfectly safe and well regulated, yet a very different picture emerges once you look into the issue. Hundreds of chemicals are used in frac'ing operations.

One Colorado study found at least 65 chemicals being used were listed as hazardous under any one of six federal state laws. A New York State study estimates 6,000 new wells over 20 years, even with frac'ing fluids using just 1% chemicals, this comes to 150 tons to 230 tons of chemicals used per day.

Public opposition in New York is so strong that it forced Chesapeake Energy  to voluntarily refrain from drilling in a lucrative region within the Marcellus Shale. In Pennsylvania, Cabot Oil & Gas  was forced to shut down their frac'ing operations in Susquehanna County and is also facing law suits claiming water contamination from frac'ing.

The US Department of Energy reports that only two-thirds of the drilling spaces have no regulation-specific hydraulic fracturing and only four have detailed regulations. There is no ETA oversight because of the highly controversial move when frac'ing was exempted from the Safe Drinking Water Act in 2005. New regulations have been introduced in New York, Pennsylvania and Colorado. The Frac Act has been introduced in Congress and the ETA has begun public hearings on hydraulic fracturing.

Some analysts predict that new regulations could add 8% to 30% to the cost of operating the well. Exxon itself included an escape clause in its merger agreement with XTO, stating that Exxon has the right to back out of the deal if federal regulations make frac'ing commercially impractical.

Yet when it comes to its shareholder, ExxonMobil  has failed to disclose the many regulatory, legal and reputational risks associated with hydraulic fracturing. In the absence of any meaningful disclosure by our company, we ask our fellow shareholders to support this proposal so that natural gas development can be done in a way that is both economically viable and without harming human health or the environment. Thank you.

Chairman Tillerson, I am [C. Barbee Gast]. I'm a professor at the University of Houston and an annuitant of the Company. And I'd like to ask a question on behalf of the shareholders interested in strategy and the future finances of the Company.

It seems, there is the appearance of a dramatic transformation in the Company in the direction of natural gas. If you look at the reserver placement, you've got like 190% reserver placement in natural gas. And in liquids it's in the 60s. And liquids production is down from where it was when we merged with mobile ten years ago.

So the question is really when you add the XTO acquisition to that, is there a rather dramatic transformation of the Company strategically going on in the direction of natural gas? And will the profitability of the future production be anything like the profitability of the more liquid space that we had in the past?

REX TILLERSON : Well, thank you for the question. In our strategic plan, we do not have a specific target in terms of our oil, gas mix holdings. We do recognize as I mentioned in the energy outlook that natural gas is going to be the fastest growing of the traditional fuels.

And so clearly a few years back, we took a view, "Well, how do we access ourselves to more natural gas resources? And how do we access natural gas resources that are close to liquid markets that have good fiscal regimes around the resources?" And that's what's led to the pursuit of the unconventionials, which are the largest growing resource in the United States and in North America.

And we have a fairly attractive fiscal regime in the United States. Our view of long-term pricing again is we don't try to forecast the price. Rather, we look at supply-demand fundamentals and we look at all of the attractive qualities of natural gas consumption relative to other options that will be available.

And so that has caused us to take a greater interest in large natural gas resources. And I say large because if they're not large, they won't be material to our results. As we announced in the XTO filing and as they have publicly disclosed, XTO currently has $45 trillion cubic feet of natural gas resources. And they have a base upon which to build that.

We have been accumulated similar types of unconventional opportunities and that's where a lot of the value we think in that transaction will be. With regard to reserve replacement, though, I think if you look over a longer period of time and as you hear my say over and over and over, we are all about the long term. But if you look at the last ten years of reserve replacement, I think you'd see that it's been fairly balanced in terms of oil and gas.

We've had some years where we have dramatically replaced oil production and did not completely replace gas production. So oftentimes this is a year-to-year effect. The years when we booked large heavy oil in oil sands, cold lake resources, coral sand resources, we had very large replacement ratios on the oil side. So it's oftentimes a function of timing.

Our strategic approach is to gain access to good quality resources, taking all those risk management factors into account. And you have to account for all of them. You can't leave any of them out. But recognize that you're in this for a very long period of time. And so even though you may either have a price environment, a political risk environment, a technology environment today that presents a hurdle to the ultimate value in that resource, we see a way forward.

We see a way, sometimes it may take six, eight, nine, 10 years to get through that, but we see a way forward where we can overcome the obstacles and then realize the value of the resource. And I would make that observation around our pursuit of resources in Iraq or our pursuit of unconventional gas resources or the oil sands or the deepwater. All of the areas where we see large, meaningful resources on offer, have something in their characteristic that presents a challenge, and the unconventionals no different.

So not a deliberate shift to gas, per se, but clearly a recognition of the important role gas will play and then therefore when we see opportunities to acquire and gain access to what we believe are going to be long-term valuable natural gas resources, we'll do that. We still do the same for oil and liquids as well.
