Good morning. I would like to cover several aspects of today's meeting. First, as we typically note at the outset of similar meetings, statements of future events or conditions included in Mr. Tillerson's remarks today are forward-looking statements. Actual future results including demand growth and mix, resource recoveries, volume growth, capital expenditures and project outcomes could differ materially due to factors discussed and those noted under the caption factors affecting future results on the investor section of our website.

I also refer you to the frequently used terms posted on our website which include definitions of some of the key financial and operating measures we will use today and additional important information.

Before we continue today, I would like to take this opportunity to familiarize everyone with the safety features of this auditorium. In case of an emergency, we will be notified through the public address system. Emergency exits for the ground level, as shown on the screen above me, are situated at the rear of the auditorium where you entered and down in front on either side. If we need to evacuate, just proceed to the nearest exit and the [Myerson] personnel will guide you to the best way out.

In addition, for safety reasons please do not stand in the aisles or at the back of the hall and please do not block the exits. To insure that the meeting is conducted in the interests of all shareholders, there are certain rules of conduct governing this meeting. These rules are posted on signs at the entrances to this meeting, are included in the program, and are shown on the screen above me. Let me cover several of the rules.

The distribution of pamphlets and other literature, banners, signs and other displays is strictly prohibited in this hall. Anyone who intentionally obstructs or interferes with this lawful meeting by physical actins or verbal utterance is in violation of Texas law. Any persons engaging in such conduct will be asked to cease and if they refuse, they will be escorted from the meeting.

The laws of New Jersey, where ExxonMobil is incorporated, provided that no business can be brought up for a vote unless proper notice has been given to all shareholders. Therefore, in fairness to other shareholders not in attendance and in keeping with the laws that govern our annual meeting, formal business at today's meeting is restricted to the items included in this year's proxy statement. Additional proposals may not be introduced from the floor.

So we can be fair to speakers and other shareholders, please turn off all cell phones and pagers. In order to present a proposal, you must have checked in at the admissions desk in the lobby and verified that you are the proponent or a representative of the proponent duly authorized under New Jersey law.

Presenters whose credentials have been verified will be given a blue presenters pass. If neither the proponent nor an authorized representative has checked in and obtained a presenters pass, we will presume the proponent is not present and I will move the proposal for the purposes of orderly conduct of the meeting and so that the shareholder votes cast may be recorded. However, I will not be acting as a representative of the proponent.

The authorized presenter of a shareholder proposal will have up to three minutes to present the proposal. Time may not be shared with another speaker. No second to the motion is required. Discussion on all items of business will be deferred until the discussion period later in the meeting.

Only shareholders, as of the record date, or their property appointed proxies are entitled to speak at this annual meeting of ExxonMobil shareholders. Shareholders making comments during the meeting must speak or have their words translated into English so that the majority of shareholders present can understand what is being said. Comments that are offensive or otherwise inappropriate will not be permitted.

We would also ask that any issues of personal interest that are not relevant to all shareholders be raised directly with the appropriate company representatives outside of the annual meeting. We request that individual shareholders respect the rights of others to speak and keep their comments as brief as possible.

As noted in the proxy statement, the chairman has broad authority to conduct the meeting in an orderly and timely manner. If you wish to make comments, you must first fill out a speaker identification card that is included in the program that was provided to you as you entered the lobby. This card confirms that you meet the requirements to speak at this meeting. Give the completed card to the usher when you are recognized to address the meeting.

To ensure as many shareholders as possible who want to address the meeting today have the opportunity to do so, we ask you to follow these additional instructions. If you would like to address the meeting, move to a reserved aisle seat and remain seated and raise your hand holding your speaker identification card to indicate to the chairman that you wish to speak. When recognized by the chairman, give your completed speaker card to the usher and the microphone will be provided. Stand and begin by stating your name. Unless otherwise provided in these rules, you may speak for us to two minutes.

Due to the large number of items on today's agenda and the need to conclude the meeting within a reasonable period of time, we cannot assure that every shareholder who wishes to speak will be able to do so. First priority will be given to those who have not yet had an opportunity to speak.

As we have done in the past, we have provided a timing system with lights that will help manage their time. I would like to demonstrate the system at this time. When the chairman recognizes a speaker and the microphone has been provided by the usher, a green light will come on at the displays on both sides of the stage. The hall microphones will be activated only after the speaker has been recognized by the chairman. When the speakers time remaining reaches 30 seconds, a yellow light will turn on. A red light will indicate the speaker is at the end of the time allowed. Thank you.

REX TILLERSON : Thank you, David. Shortly we will address our items of business. However, before doing so I'd like to share with you some highlights from the year 2010 including our financial and operating results and describe the areas which position ExxonMobil to meet the world's growing need for energy.

Your companies advantages are grounded in a commitment to integrity, risk management and financial discipline and continue to distinguish ExxonMobil from others and they provide us with the foundation to deliver ongoing value to you, our shareholders over the long term. First, let me cover a few of our financial and operating results. I'm pleased to report to you solid performance in the year 2010 across all key measures and in all of our business lines.

First, and most importantly, we had a good year of operational excellence, including industry leading safety performance and strong environmental management and progress. We delivered exceptional financial and operating results, including earnings of $30.5 billion, upstream volume growth of 13% and a return on average capital employed of 22%.

We maintained our program of selective investments with CapEx of $32 billion in 2010, a record level of capital spending. Shareholder distributions were nearly $20 billion and contributed to a total shareholder return of over 10%. We again added more oil and natural gas reserves than we produced, marking the 17th consecutive year our reserve replacement rate has exceeded 100%. These results are a tribute to the hard work, diligence and focus of the more than 80,000 men and women who work on ExxonMobil 's behalf the world over.

Now I'll review our safety and environmental performance. As many of you have heard me say before, nothing receives more management attention at ExxonMobil than the safety and health of our employees, our contractors, our customers and the people who live and work in the areas where we operate.

Our vision that nobody gets hurt is internalized in the Company's culture and is a central, critical element of daily operational excellence. Our safety performance continues to lead the industry and we are proud of this achievement. In 2010 we achieved our best ever lost time incident rates for our combined employee and contractor workforce, improving upon our record performance of 2009.

Within ExxonMobil we know good safety performance leads to good business performance. Safety and operational risk management are at the center of decision making at all times and at every level of the organization. We know that a strong safety culture has a positive influence on the behavior of each employee and contractor.

Let's now look at environmental performance. Meeting the world's growing need for energy while managing environmental risk to minimize impacts both immediate and longer term is a significant challenge. Within in ExxonMobil we have developed and implemented rigorous environmental management programs that deliver ongoing improvement in our global, environmental performance.

One such area of particular attention is emissions reduction through improved energy efficiency by applying our global energy management system, we are on target to improve energy efficiency across our worldwide refining and petro chemical operations by at least 10% between the period from the years 2002 to 2012.

We also continue to make progress reducing hydrocarbon flaring associated with our operations. In 2010 upstream hydrocarbon flaring was 20% lower than in 2009 and was down almost 60% from levels only a few years ago. Through these two efforts alone, flare reduction and energy efficiency, we have reduced greenhouse gas emissions by 12 million metric tons compared to the year 2006, which is equivalent to taking 2.5 million cars off the road in the United States.

I'm also pleased to report that in 2010 our marine organizations had no hydrocarbon spills from company owned and operated vessels nor from term chartered vessels. This represents four years since we last experienced any spill associated with our company owned and operated marine transport activities. We also reduced the number of spills not from marine vessels achieving our best ever results.

Let's now look at 2010 financial and operating results. ExxonMobil earned $30.5 billion in 2010, an increase of 57% from 2009. These results which led the industry included a record year for earnings from our chemicals business. With relentless focus on operational excellence delivering strong reliability we continue to maximize the value of our broad base of assets. We also maintained record levels of investment as shown on this next slide.

In 2010 we invested $32 billion in capital and exploration expenditures, an amount exceeding our earnings to position the business for long term growth. During the past five years we have invested over $126 billion sustaining our pursuit of attractive opportunities throughout the business cycle. We pursue opportunities in all regions of the world and across all our business lines. In 2010 we completed three major upstream projects with 2011 forecast production of about 120,000 barrels a day equivalent.

Our approach is to selectively invest in attractive opportunities that will provide acceptable returns across a broad range of industry and market conditions. This disciplined approach to investing and our emphasis on capital efficiency have consistently yielded industry leading returns.

We continue to view return on average capital employed as the best measure of capital productivity. In 2010 ExxonMobil 's return on capital employed was an industry leading 22%, more than 4 percentage points higher than our nearest competitor. Over the five year period of 2006 to 2010, our ROCE averaged above 27%, over 7 percentage points higher than the nearest competitor.

We manage each of our business lines for the long term, consistently executing our business model across the upstream, the downstream and our chemicals businesses. As a result, 2006 to 2010 average ROCE remains ahead of competition in each of our business lines as well, reflecting the strength of our integrated portfolio. Once we have met all operating cost obligations and funded all attractive investment opportunities, we return the excess cash to you, our shareholders.

We have maintained our approach to dividends with a view to build long term shareholder value and provide reliable dividend growth, not just through the good times, but also through the difficult times.

Over the past five years we distributed almost $40 billion in dividends to shareholders. During this same period, we increased per share dividends 53%. Since 1983 through multiple business cycle expansions and contractions, shareholders have received yearly dividend increases at an annualized per share growth rate of 5.7%, almost twice the rate of inflation.

In addition to growing dividends, we have provided added flexibility and returns to shareholders via our share repurchase program. In 2010 we distributed over $11 billion to shareholders through share purchases while competitor programs were curtailed for much, if not all, of the year.

On a cumulative basis, distributions to shareholders through share purchases were $114 billion over the last five years, more than twice the total distributed by our competitors. Purchases have reduced shares outstanding by almost 19% since the beginning of the year 2006, including the impacts of the shares issued for the XTO merger. This results in an average annual yield uplift of 5.6%.

We continue to believe the share purchase program is an effective away to distribute value to shareholders while maintaining the flexibility to balance the cash needs of the corporation. As a result of share buyback program, each share of ExxonMobil has an interest in 28% more production volumes today than it did in 2006, comparing these results to our competition reinforces the beneficial effect of the share purchase program for our shareholders.

Since 2006 ExxonMobil has delivered annualized all equivalent production per share growth of 6.3%, more than two percentage points higher than our nearest competitor. Share repurchases have had a similar ownership concentration effect on reserves growth. Each share of ExxonMobil has an interest in over 32% more reserves today than in 2006. Since 2006, ExxonMobil has delivered annualized reserves per share growth of over 7%, nearly 4 percentage points higher than our nearest competitor.

The combination of ExxonMobil 's industry leading business results and share purchase program represent a powerful and prudent approach to delivering shareholder value. This value is further reflected in earnings per share.

In 2010 earnings per share were $6.24, demonstrating strong underlying business performance. The bars on the left show the cumulative impact of the share purchase program on earnings per share since Exxon and Mobil merged. Earnings per share in 2010 were 42% higher than would be the case if 2010 earnings were divided by the number of shares outstanding in the year 2000, the first year of the merger. And this is across a decade of record capital investments and opportunities that will deliver earnings and cash flow for years into the future.

Importantly, we have maintained this approach through each business cycle, again the good times or the tough times. Now each year, I think most of you know we take a broad in depth look at the global energy marketplace and we author a comprehensive report entitled the outlook for energy, which we make available to the public. This report describes our view on the long term trends in energy and it serves importantly as a foundation for our future business plans.

Using the year 2005 as a baseline, in the period to the year 2030, we anticipate that expanding prosperity for a growing world population is going to drive increasing global energy demand of almost 35%. To meet these growing needs and insure reliable and affordable energy, the world must pursue a diverse mix of commercially viable energy sources. The bar chart on the left shows projected demand growth from 2005 to 2030 by energy type.

In 2005 oil, natural gas and coal provided approximately 80% of the world's energy. Nuclear, hydroelectric, geothermal, biomass, along with wind, solar and biofuels contributed to balance. The global energy mix will continue to shift and evolve between now and the next 20 years. Natural gas will be the fastest growing major energy source and will overtake coal as the second largest global energy source behind only oil. Growth of this reliable, affordable and clean fuel is aided by technologies that have unlocked vat new supplies to meet a wide variety of needs, perhaps most notably for power generation.

We expect continued emphasis in developed countries toward reduced greenhouse gas emissions as an abundant and relatively lower carbon intensive fuel, natural gas is well suited to support those objectives.

Our outlook anticipates that energy efficiency, long and important element in modulating energy demand growth, will continue to play an increasing role in moderating future demand throughout the world. The bar on the right shows the energy saved through projected efficiency gains is expected to be about twice the projected growth in global energy consumption. Without these efficiency gains, total energy demand will be much higher in the year 2030.

As mentioned, natural gas is expected to be the fastest growing major fuel source, increasing about 60% globally by the year 2030. On the left is depicted our view of US natural gas supply and demand. We expect US domestic gas production to increase on the strength of unconventional gas resources. These significant new supplies from shell gas and tight gas resources will be required to offset the ongoing declines in t he conventional sources of US natural gas.

The chart in the middle of the slide depicts the gas outlook for Europe, with domestic production falling, Europe will be required to meet its demand growth with a combination of imports via pipelines from Russia, the Caspian region, and North Africa as well as a growing level of imported liquefied natural gas.

Finally, the chart on the right describes the Asia Pacific region where demand in 2030 will be approaching three times the level of the year 2005. This rising demand will be met by growth in local conventional and unconventional supplies as well as increasing supplies of LNG and pipeline imports. ExxonMobil is favorably positioned in each of these markets with supplies from our diverse global gas portfolio of high quality conventional, liquefied natural gas and unconventional resources.

The growing global demand for energy and related products presents important challenges. In the decades ahead, the world would need to expand supplies in a way that is safe, secure, affordable and environmentally responsible. The scale of the challenge is enormous and requires an integrated set of solutions and the pursuit of all economic options.

A commitment to the devilment and deployment of new energy technologies to expand supply of traditional fuels and advance new energy resources will require unprecedented levels of investment. We also know from experience that our shared goals can only be met by effectively identifying and managing the risk inherent to our business activities and by maintaining a relentless focus on operational excellence.

ExxonMobil has established competitive advantages that are apparent across all three of our major business lines. These competitive advantages set us apart and have not only led to superior performance but also serve as the foundation for our ongoing success.

Within each of our businesses, the quality, size and diversity of our balanced portfolio of resources, projects, products and assets is unparalleled. Our investment programs are underpinned by high impact technologies that enable us to manage risk and maximize resource value. We maintain ongoing research and development programs to identify and develop new technologies that enable us to be more efficient and more effective.

With a relentless focus on operational excellence we develop and deploy systems that insure consistent approaches across the globe to insure us the highest operating standards. These competitive advantages are under pinned by effective risk management and position ExxonMobil to meet these daunting energy challenges.

At over 84 billion oil equivalent barrels, ExxonMobil has the largest resource base among the international oil companies. In 2010 we increased the resource base by nearly 10 billion oil equivalent barrels with organic growth by the bit and through attractive acquisitions. The depth and diversity of the resource base supports a significant upstream portfolio of projects.

The bar on the left describes the resource base by type of technological approach that is necessary to bring the resources to production. The largest two segments are conventional oil and gas and heavy oil and oil sounds, which include both in situ and oil mining processes. Our position in unconventional gas and oil is also substantial as a result of the addition of XTO. The remainder is comprised of resources with high content levels of acid and sour components, liquefied natural gas, arctic resources and resources located in deep water.

As shown in t he middle bar, just over 50% of our resource base is located in the Americas, with the remainder distributed around the world. The resource base is also evenly balanced between liquids and natural gas as indicated in the bar on the right. These are the resources from which our upstream investment opportunities are developed. And I'll take a quick step through some of the projects and operations underway starting with conventional resources.

A high quality portfolio of conventional assets continues to provide a strong foundation for our overall asset base and it serves as a place to develop many of our operating practices, which allow us to compete for new opportunities. For example, early last year ExxonMobil signed a 25 year agreement with the government of Iraq which includes development of discovered undeveloped and underdeveloped reservoirs in the West Qurna phase one license area. We're bringing to bear our global experience in project execution, production enhancement, and facility and operations integrity to support this work effort. We also continue to apply new innovative approaches enabled by leading edge technologies to conventional assets to maximize their value.

ExxonMobil is working as part of the ZADCO operating company in Abu Dhabi to develop the upper Zakum field's extensive oil resources through an innovative approach, the creation or artificial islands where drilling rigs and processing facilities are co-located. With our partners, we developed a plan for the creation of three islands which are now under construction. This innovative approach has enabled us to increase the ultimate recovery from the reservoir, saving billions of dollars on the project as well as dramatically reducing the environmental footprint.

We hold significant high quality heavy oil and oil sands resources. The Cold Lake field in Alberta Canada is the largest thermal in situ heavy oil project in the world. Our experience in Cold Lake and the Syncrude oil sands mining and upgrading operation serve as a foundation of future developments. New projects at both locations are in the planning phase or are underway to further expand development of these already producing and high quality resources.

The Kearl Oil Sands project, north east of the syncrude project is developing a world class resource in northern Alberta which is expected to exceed 4 billion barrels of oil. Construction and fabrication activities are underway on the initial development project with mining and extraction facilities scheduled for completion next year. We also continue to evaluate our extensive oil sands acreage positions in the broader Athabasca region, core hole and seismic programs continue in both in situ and mining leases.

In 2010 ExxonMobil established a material position in North America unconventional resources with the merger of XTO. The successful conclusion of the merger has positioned us to pursue other attractive unconventional resources. The subsequent acquisitions of the Ellora properties in the Haynesville and the Petrohawk properties in the Fayetteville shale added low cost exposure to these important plays to our now leading global unconventional portfolio of natural gas and unconventional oil resources, which totals now over 100 trillion cubic feet equivalent.

With the leadership position in multiple unconventional plays, ExxonMobil is the largest producer of natural gas in the United States and we are positioned to double our US unconventional production over the next decade with an inventory of approximately 50,000 drillable well locations.

With this established technical and operating capability in the United States, we are also well positioned to support the pursuit of a diverse global portfolio that includes emerging unconventional resource opportunities in Canada, South America, Europe and Southeast Asia. Through these pursuits we presently have access to more than 10 million net acres globally.

Technology is enabling economic development of acid sour resources. In 2010 a demonstration plant was commissioned at the shoot creek Wyoming facility in the LaBarge field. This plant will test our proprietary controlled free zone technology by using a single step cryogenic separation process, this technology could dramatically lower the cost of removing CO2 and hydrogen sulfide from natural gas. The technology may also have application in carbon capture and storage approaches to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Development planning continues on technical and execution access -- aspects for the Natuna D Alpha block project in Indonesia. This is a large 46 trillion cubic foot offshore gas field containing over 70% carbon dioxide.

In 2010 ExxonMobil signed the heads of agreement with Pertamina , the Indonesian national oil company which provides a framework for negotiation of a new production sharing contract with the government of Indonesia. We also continue to work with partners to progress the phase development of the massive Kashagen oil field, located offshore Kazakhstan in the Caspian Sea.

Over the past decade, ExxonMobil has built a substantial, global liquefied natural gas portfolio. In Qatar we continue to work with Qatar petroleum to develop the north field, the world's largest non associated gas field. In 2009 and 2010 our joint venture started up four of the world's largest LNG trains, each with a production capacity of 7.8 million tons per year. The projects are well positioned to supply LNG to major markets in Asia, Europe and North America.

As part of our global joint LNG supply chain with Qatar, the golden pass LNG regasification terminal in Sabine Pass Texas was commissioned and received its first LNG cargo from Qatar in 2010. We are extending our LNG project expertise and experience to develop other new projects in Papua New Guinea and to participate with our partners in the Gorgon Jansz LNG project in Australia.

We also have world class -- a world class portfolio of oil and gas opportunities located in the arctic. In far east Russia the latest phase of the Sakhalin 1 project, Odoptu, started up in 2010 with average production of more than 50,000 barrels per day gross. The Odoptu development utilized the Yastreb rig, one of the world's most powerful onshore drilling rigs to drill seven extended reach wells from the shore side to bottom hoe locations up to seven miles offshore, setting new world records for reach and length.

The next phase of the Sakhalin 1 development is the Arkutun-Dagi oil development. Major contracts have been awarded and construction is underway on the offshore, ice resistant gravity based structure. This development will require approximately 45 wells and expected to yield peak production of 90,000 barrels per day gross start up of Arkutun-Dagi is anticipated in 2014.

And finally, we recently awarded the Hebron offshore topside and gravity based structure front end engineering and design contracts. The Hebron and Hibernia southern extension projects offshore eastern Canada will develop over 750 million oil equivalent barrels contributing a peak production of 180,000 barrels a day gross. Extensive arctic experience and capability positions us well to advance Hebron and the development of several satellite resources offshore eastern Canada.

We continue to hold a strong position in the deep water. The Kizomba satellites phase one project in Angola is expected to produce an additional 100,000 barrels per day gross. The project includes subsea tie backs to the existing Kizomba A and B floating production storage and offloading vessels. Execution activities are progressing toward an anticipated start up around the mid part of next year.

We also have an extensive acreage position in the US Gulf of Mexico, which totals 2.1 million net acres and includes exposure to multiple plays. Following a gas discovery at the Keathley Canyon at the Hadrian South location we met a large oil discovery last year at Hadrian North and we have recently resumed drilling to continue appraisal of the Hadrian complex. In the western gulf we have acquired and are processing new large scale wide azimuth surveys as we actively build our prospect inventory. As you can see, we have a diverse global portfolio of high quality upstream resources with a very strong inventory of projects, and operational excellence supporting robust oil and gas production growth.

Upstream volumes grew an impressive 13% in 2010, driven by superior organic of 6% from project startups and strong operational performance across the upstream. The ongoing successful integration of XTO's world class unconventional operations added another 7%. As the largest nongovernment owned producer of oil and gas with volumes of 4.5 million oil equivalent barrels produced per day, these increases were the most significant among our competitors and exceeded the competitor average by 12 percentage points.

Now, let's take a closer look at the downstream portfolio. In the downstream ExxonMobil is the largest global integrated refiner. Our refineries on average are 60% larger than the industry, providing us with scale advantages. We're also the largest manufacturer of lubricant base stocks as well as a leading marketer of petroleum products.

Our refineries are among the most efficient in their geographies as a result of a constant focus on energy and cost efficiencies, circuit optimization and reliability operations. We also capture significant value by running challenged crudes, which are typically discounted in the market, allowing us to reduce fee stock costs and increasing our margins.

Enabled by our virtual molecular assays and capital investments to expand fee flexibility, we are processing over 60% more challenged crudes than the industry average, lowering our cost of supply to our refineries. Our branded retail businesses are well known with transportation and fuel products sold through our world class ExxonMobil and SO brands. The pie diagram shows the broad spectrum of sales channels for our fuels marketing business and represents about 3.7 million barrels per day in total sales.

The business to business portion of our portfolio, which includes industrial and wholesale, marine and aviation is a significant contributor. Business to business makes up over 50% of total fuels marketing sales while employing a very low capital base. Fuels marketing business has diverse channels that are integrated with our refineries, our high quality products coupled with a strong refining and distribution network position us as a reliable supplier to a wide variety of customers around the world.

In the high value finished lubricants business our flagship passenger vehicle engine oil, Mobil 1, continued to achieve record sales growth in 2010. Through technology and brand leadership we have captured significantly higher sales growth in the industry. The Mobil SHC brand of synthetic industrial oils has also captured significant growth in recent years as customers are choosing to protect their industrial equipment and to increase productivity by using our differentiated products and lubrication engineering services.

By leveraging equipment builder relationships and efficient global business models we have established a significant growth business in the developing markets such as China, India and Russia at rates considerably faster than our competitors. The strength of our brands and technology coupled with a reliable efficient supply chain will enable us to continue to capture superior growth in the future.

Now I'd like to take a quick look at the chemicals business. Our unique chemical portfolio mix captures the benefits of scale and commodities chemicals while maximizing the value from specialty products where we hold the number one or number two market position in all products. Our world scale commodity businesses, shown in red, capture upside earnings when margins are strong. Specialties, shown in blue, provide a stable yet growing earnings base that delivered a record $1.8 billion last year, contributing to a record almost $5 billion in total from chemical earnings in 2010.

Our diverse product portfolio is backed by proprietary technology in areas such as advantaged feed stocks, lower cot manufacturing and premium products. The ability to consistently deliver strong results from commodities and specialties positions ExxonMobil Chemical to significantly out form the competition. Our sustained commitment to technology is a significant competitive advantage. We pursue constant innovation to improve the supply of reliable, affordable energy in a safe and environmentally responsible manner.

Over the past five years we have invested approximately $4.5 billion in research and development activities in support of our business functions. This commitment to research and development through the business cycle supports technology extensions to support our immediate and our near tem business objectives. Our research programs also support pursuit of technology breakthroughs, which will be important to our longer term strategic objectives. We recognize over time break through technologies do become the industry standard as energy sources that were once considered unreachable become mainstream.

An example of one breakthrough strategic research project we've undertake is our partnership with Synthetics Genomics Incorporated in the development of advanced algae-based biofuels. We believe there are numerous potential benefits of biofuel production from algae that make this option a more attractive choice over the other types of biofuels.

Through the natural process of photosynthesis, algeas consume carbon dioxide and convert it to useful products like oils and oxygen. Biofuels made form plants like corn and sugarcane can and do impact global food supplies by utilizing fertile land and fresh water for fuel instead of food.

Algae on the other hand, can be grown using land unsuitable for food production and can thrive in treated wastewaters, saltwater and brackish water. Algae are also highly productive with the potential to yield greater volumes per acre than any other biofuel source and unlike other crops, can be grown year round in special manmade ponds or enclosed in photo bioreactors exposed to abundant sunlight.

Algae based biofuels can also be more easily integrated within the current infrastructure of fuels distribution and within the existing fleet of vehicles. This research and development program involves multiple phases, each with its own unique set of challenges with continued progress though, we expect to spend about $600 million assuming the project milestones are met.

In most of the areas in which we compete, ExxonMobil is considered the premiere organization. Our disciplined approach to operations and investments enable us -- each of our businesses to generate strong returns. We're the largest producer of liquids among major integrated oil companies and we're well positioned for future growth with our high quality, low cost oil sands project at Kearl. With our world class investments in Qatar and future LNG projects, we're among the leaders in the LNG value chain. With the acquisition of XTO and our growing unconventional portfolio around the world, we have created the premiere unconventional gas company.

In the downstream, not only are we the largest global refiner, we also stand as the number one supplier of lubricant base stocks. We also have the highest return chemical company and the competitions not even close as we generate returns more than two and a half times greater than our nearest competitor. The value -- the sum of the different parts of our business is significant, if not always recognized as evidenced by our leadership in the areas in which we compete. However, we manage the corporation to capture the sum of the parts plus. At ExxonMobil we leverage financial strength, rigorous management systems and operating synergies to capture additional value for shareholders across our businesses through the integration processes.

The industry faces multiple uncertainties and inherent risk. First and foremost are risks associated with safety, security, health and the environment. Over the years the industry has seen examples where the failure to effectively manage these risks has resulted in serious, even tragic consequences, including the loss of life and harm to the environment. Additionally, there are significant financial, economic and commercial risks associated with the very large and growing capital investments required to develop increasingly complex oil and gas projects.

The recovery of resources located miles beneath the surface of the earth also carries a wide range of technical risk involving many geological and engineering complexities. Given that these projects are executed in many countries around the world and often operate for several decades, there's the associated geopolitical risk as governments and political priorities change, often within the lifecycle of one project.

Finally, t he industry is faced with risk of climate change and the resulting effect of government policies and impact on global markets. Well developed processes procedures and people are required to manage all of these risks.

Over many decades ExxonMobil has established common worldwide expectations for addressing the risk inherent in our business. These expectations are fully embedded in our culture and we remain focused on continuously improving our ability to effectively identify and manage risk across all of our business activities. First, a capable committed workforce with clear accountability is important since human decision making is a significant component of successful risk management.

We develop our employees to have the highest technical and leadership skills in the industry, which creates a sustainable source of advantage. This is supported by well developed and clearly defined policies and procedures to insure that we have a structured, globally consistent approach with the highest standards in place. These high standards are rigorously applied at the design stage to reduce and eliminate risk where possible. Additionally, employee and contractor training is an essential element to insure support at all levels within the organization and to embed the right behaviors. We employ a systematic approach to measuring performance and seeking continuous improvement across our business.

This is all achieved within the context of rigorously applied risk management systems. ExxonMobil utilizes a comprehensive set of systems to manage the risk. Recognized as a model of success in the industry ExxonMobil developed the operations integrity management system, or OIMS, to provide a robust framework for managing safety, security, health and environmental risk. OIMS is employed in our facilities worldwide and enables us to measure progress, insure management accountability for results and establish common worldwide expectations for controlling operational risk.

Facility integrity management systems are employed to prevent high impact equipment and facility failures and to improve equipment reliability. The benefits are significant and have resulted in material reductions and unscheduled downtime. The controls integrity management system, or CIMS, provides a structured common process for conducting business in a well controlled manner. This includes establishing effective business controls, monitoring and enforcing compliance continuously and resolving control weaknesses in a timely manner.

ExxonMobil 's capital project management system, EMCAPS uses management gate reviews and checkpoints to insure that projects are conducted in a safe and environmentally responsible manner. That they deliver assets of an appropriate quality meeting cost and scheduled expectations and achieve commercial success.

We have additional management systems that we employ to mitigate the many risks we face, including the oversight of assets that are operated by others. We believe that the frameworks in place at ExxonMobil provide us a unique competitive advantage to managing the broad array of risk before us. Now, I'd like to let a few representatives from our global workforce speak to you about operational excellence, including our approach to risk management and safety.

The most powerful commercial entity in the world meets just once a year with those to whom it is legally accountable. title: Exxon Mobil Corp Shareholders Meeting
name: MICHELLE MILLER
speaker: Investor
text:
Good morning, Mr. Chairman, board of directors and fellow shareholders. My name is Michelle Miller and I am representing the Laborers National Pension Fund. As long term shareholders of Exxon we support transparency and accountability in corporate spending on political activities. These include activities considered intervention any political campaign under the internal revenue code, such as direct or indirect political contributions to candidates, political parties or political organizations, independent expenditures, or electioneering communications on behalf of federal, state or local candidates

Disclosure is consistent with public policy in the best interest of the Company and its shareholders and critical for the compliance with federal ethics laws. Moreover, the Supreme Court's citizens united decision recognized the importance of political spending disclosure for shareholders when it said disclosures permits citizens and shareholders to react to the speech of corporate entities in a proper way. This transparency enables the electorate to make informed decisions and give proper weight to different speakers and messages.

Gaps in transparency and accountability may expose the Company to reputational and business risks that could threaten the long term shareholder value.

We would like to stress that even when a company is confident that its political activities are in compliance with the law it must determine whether the political spending actually advances the Company's interest. For example, in August of 2010, Target Corporation made a political contribution of $150,000 to MN Ford, a group that was backing a gubernatorial candidate that was opposed to gay and immigration rights. Following much public criticism and boycott threats, Target, a company known for its support of diversity and gay rights had to issue a public apology.

In the meantime, the Company's brand suffered significant damage. Our proposal simply protects the Company and its long term shareholders from corporate decision makings that could result in a similar reputational risk. The proposal asks the Company to disclose all of its political spending, including payments to trade associations and other tax exempt organizations for political purposes.

This would bring our company in line with a growing number of leading companies including Aetna , American Electric Power and Microsoft that support political disclosure and accountability and presents its information on their website. The Company's board and its shareholders need complete disclosure to be -- to be fully able to evaluate the political use of its corporate assets. Failure to do so could result in public embarrassments. Thus, we urge your support for this critical governance reform. Thank you.

Rather a full policy on support of the human right to water would address the ways in which the Company's business [daily news] from manufacturing processes to product use. In fact, all people's access to safe, sufficient, acceptable, physically accessible and aportable water locally and in the international community.

Without such a policy, we are concerned that the Company may mean shareholder value may be at risk as broader enforcement and regulations of the human right to water grows internationally.

Shareholders believe that ExxonMobil should join these other major corporations who identified the human right to water as a real concern to both their company and the communities in which they do business. speaker: Investor
text:
Good morning. My name is Gary Matthews and I am here on behalf of Green Century Capital Management to present item number nine, report on Canadian oil sands. This resolution requests that the board of directors of ExxonMobil prepare a thorough report discussing possible long term risks to the Company's finances and operations posed by the environmental, social and economic challenges associated with the oil sands.

Mining upgrading and refining by [Tumin] from oil sands is one of the most environmentally costly sources of transport fuel in the world, highly resource intensive and environmentally damaging, requiring the draining of wetlands, diversion of rivers, creation of massive toxic taling ponds and the removal of trees and vegetation, on top of the impacts on air quality, water quality, wildlife and ecosystems, oil sands re also incredibly energy intensive and their development and expansion will mean a significant increase in greenhouse gas emissions.

ExxonMobil has dramatically increased investments in the oil sands over recent years through its stake in imperial oil and through ExxonMobil Canada. In 2011 Exxon's total proved resources in the oil sands and heavy oil were 21% of its entire resource base according to the chart we saw earlier. Due to its carbon intensive products and long term capital horizons the oil sands sector is uniquely exposed to the economic, competitive and regulatory risk resulting from oil price volatility and other related market forces.

As a result, investors and independent analysts have raised doubts about the long term economic viability of oil sands development. Recently, ExxonMobil has increased its reporting on this oil sands operations, but its existing disclosure does not satisfy the central focus of this proposal, potential long term risks posed to the Company's operations and finances resulting from its oil sands operations.

At the same time, the Company lags behind its peers in disclosing the environmental, social and economic risks it might face because of its presence in the Canadian oil sands. We believe that given the unique economic challenges inherent to oil sands development more disclosure is necessary to provide investors information on how Exxon is managing associated risks.

In short, we simply want to know more about how the elaborate risk management systems mentioned earlier are applied specifically to the oil sands projects. In the absence of meaningful disclosure, shareholders have no way of knowing if ExxonMobil is addressing these significant risks. As a result, we cannot be assured that our shareholder value is fully protected. Therefore we urge you to vote for, in support of, item number nine, report on Canadian oil sands. Thank you.

title: Exxon Mobil Corp Shareholders Meeting
name: CRAIG ROSEBROWN
speaker: Investor
text:
Mr. Tillerson, board, fellow shareholders. My name is [Craig Rosebrown] I'm a shareholder from out west and my question revolves around the proposal number 12 I believe, the green house gas emissions. I'm a filmmaker and an author and as part of a group that has traveled around the world looking at different communities and how they've been affected by the impacts of human cause climate change.

Now ExxonMobil , I believe, it was around 2008 made a commitment to stop funding denialist organizations and scientists whose purpose was to cast doubt on the reality of climate change and yet, in very recent news coming out of the United Kingdom, investigators showed that ExxonMobil was still funding some of these denialist organizations.

So my question to you, Mr. Tillerson, in this now 2011 when there is consensus among the international scientific community that human cause climate change is a real threat that needs to be remedied, an action needs to be taken, will you make a personal promise on behalf of ExxonMobil to do what you can to stop funding denialist organizations and admit once and for all that human cause climate change is real and ExxonMobil is going to lead the way to do something about it.

REX TILLERSON : Well, I'd be happy to respond to your question. I think our positions, we hope, have been made as clear as we're able to make them. That we view the risk from climate change as serious and it's a risk that does need to be managed in a very broad and global way. That trying to manage that risk --anyone country trying to manage that risk or certainly anyone state trying to manage that risk is unlikely to produce any meaningful impact.

We do contribute to the broad based understand of the science underlying climate change and we have funded efforts on all sides of that issue at both the academic level and at private institutions because we think it's important on a policy that has such far reaching and dramatic impacts on society and our economic performance not just in this country but for the world, that we have the most fulsome discussion of what we understand bout this very complicated issue. The science community, you're correct, shares a consensus that this is a serious risk.

There is a consensus that human activity without question contributes to that risk, but there is also recognition that the complexities of climate science involve many elements that are still not well understood by the scientific community. And it is important if we are going to formulate policies around the human component of that challenge that we understand what is the impact of those policies going to be. Are they going to produce a measureable benefit or are they not?

And in order to do that, it means you have to understand other elements of the climate system that the science communities quite frankly struggles with still today. And so we continue to fund a number of activities to better help the scientific community hopefully better understand this very complicated climate system. Very elegant climate system that we enjoy on planet earth.

So I think oftentimes people view that funding as somehow funding people who don't believe in a particular position around the direct effect of human contribution. I don't think any of us have ever suggested that we don't believe human activity contributes. The question is, we all also know and the scientific community knows there are a lot of other things going on.

So good policy we have always said, needs to be under pinned by the very best scientific understanding we can have. And our approach, I hope, is well understood is that this is a serious risk, you can't wait until you have the 100% certain answer to begin to deal with it. So you do the things, we have supported policies that we know move us in the right direction and that's why we have been longer proponent of energy efficiency and ways in which the market can help people make better decisions about their activities that are associated with greenhouse gas emissions.

And as Sister Pat noted, we have said in the policy debate that if governments are looking for policy alternatives to influence human behavior choices in the products and services and the way they carry out their activities that we believe the carbon tax is the most effective way to allow people the freedom to choose how they want to modify their lifestyle, as posed to systems of cap in trade which as we model them, we do not believe ultimately produced the most economically efficiency outcome of shifting behavior.

It is an area of enormous concern. It's an area of enormous debate, witness the various meetings of the IPCC and the intergovernmental groups trying to deal with this. And what I can tell you is while there are certainly consensus among the scientific community of the problem, the risks that are involved and that human activities contribute, there's a wide range of variability in the science community of the understanding of just how much you attribute to each of those activities and therefore there is also a wide range of variability as to what governments feel is the appropriate approach in the global community.

What I'll commit to you is we're going to continue to be actively engaged in that discussion and that debate. We are the only industrial company -- the only industrial company that has had a science representative on the IPCC committee from the beginning. Only ExxonMobil . So I assume we are -- have been engaged in that discussion. We take it very seriously. We fund a lot of activities to try and contribute to a better understanding of the problem and a better understanding of policies that are going to have to play out over the next one to 200 years. So that's what I can commit to you we will do in response to your question.

title: Exxon Mobil Corp Shareholders Meeting
name: MOLLY ROOKE
speaker: Investor
text:
I'm Molly Rooke, and I wanted to make a comment regarding item number 10 on the hydraulic fracturing. I live here in Dallas and I'm real familiar with what's been going on here in the Barnet Shale and the problems with the hydraulic fracturing and the shale gas drilling and have been reading a whole lot about what's going on around the country and I was reading the arguments that have been made here on the proxy statement to vote against this proposal stating that hydraulic fracturing is highly regulated at the state level to effectively protect drinking water wells and ground water aquifers.

If that were so, we wouldn't be having all the problems that we're having both here and around the country and I know certainly that this is not highly regulated in Texas and problems with drinking water have been huge and it's still being studied what all the problems are that are contributing to this. But what is known and its directly related to the hydraulic fracturing process because people are having perfectly clean drinkable water before it and then right after it happens they no longer have drinkable safe water, they have methane in their homes that make their houses unsafe to live in and can contribute to explosions in their houses.

Their water can catch on fire, ridiculous things that are actually happening. I know people who have had this. People who have also had the -- fracking fluids that have gotten out onto their property and had their pet dogs killed from drinking it, have livestock killed. There are serious problems going on with this.

I know it's a process that's old, but there're things as you know that are new that are going on and I encourage ExxonMobil to do everything they can to employ the best procedures and practices and technologies that are available including for air quality, because still there's so many emissions from VOCs and other emissions, methane and other that are contributing not only to toxic air emissions, but to air emissions that are contributing to high ozone.

Like in the Dallas Fort Worth area there are studies that shows that the emissions from the hydraulic fracturing, shale gas drilling is contributing more than our auto emissions in this area. And that's a huge change and there are problems with ozone in rural areas now that had perfectly clean air before the shale gas drilling and so that's definitely the contributor to it. And, as you know, there are technologies available. I know that ExxonMobil can do better and I hope that they will in this developing energy source, especially as it continues to grow. So thank you.

REX TILLERSON : Thank you. I might just offer a couple of comments. As you pointed out, hydraulic fracturing deals -- there are a lot of risks you have to mange with it but the three that you listed, the fracturing process itself not being contained within the well bore and the zone such that it contaminates shallow or fresh water zones, the handling of produced water and fluids when they come back and then the emissions from the production operations, whether they be from tank emissions or from compressors that are used.

I want to assure you we understand all of those risks very well and I -- and I don't necessarily agree with your comment that it's not highly regulated. In the state of Texas the railroad commission has had long standing rules that deal with all three of those issues. Now, as the activity levels have picked up, we agree and we've been engaged in active participation to look at the rules to see how we can make those rules more responsive to some of the concerns and insure that all of the participants in the industry are operating at a standard that we all would expect.

The contamination of fresh water -- shallow water zones from the hydraulic fracturing process has yet to be substantiated in any case. They -- we are now in the third study by the environmental protection agency over the last 10 years. The prior two studies concluded no contamination cases were ever substantiated.

Now, that doesn't mean there's not natural gas in fresh water zones and I know -- because you study this you know all this that I'm saying, but natural gas can occur in fresh water zones biogenic gas naturally or it could be there from contamination related to drilling processes decades ago, because in Texas in particular we've been an oil and gas producing state for more than 100 years, a lot of wells drilled in some of these areas and as producing activities occur -- and I'm talking about producing the ground water, the fresh water, because in the Dallas Fort Worth area there have been an enormous number of freshwater wells drilled by individuals and agriculture.

And so there's a lot of fresh water being removed from the aquifers and if there has been historic contamination that can cause that gas to move around as wells are produced. So oftentimes where there may not have been gas it may migrate to a location where there's a lot of ground water extraction and I only say that to make this point. There are a lot of -- there are a lot of things going on in fresh water aquifers, some of which is related to long ago contamination that occurred in drilling operations decades ago and its resident, it's there, and it may from time to time appear. Some of it is naturally occurring.

The regulator does have procedures in place, one to insure we protect those zones and second that when there is contamination that we verify to the best of our capabilities where that may have come from and so I assure you it's an issue that we manage seriously. The water handling issue at the surface is one that the industry continues to improve its practices with a larger and larger percentage of that water being recycled. Because water is an expensive part of the process for us.

So we are highly incentivized to try and capture and reuse as much of that as possible. And I think in the air emissions question there is a survey, as you know, that's been going on in some of the urban areas to fully understand what is the contribution to VOCs and other emissions in the area from the oil and gas activities. And we -- we support and agree. We need to go out and get data. There's an awful lot of conclusive statements being made that for which there is no comprehensive data to support those.

So we support getting that data, lets fully understand it and then you're right, we have solutions to once we understand what the problem is and what our contribution may be and we're going to -- again, we're going to to be active in that read because obviously we have taken an enormous position in the unconditional space because of our belief that this is a resource that is vital to America's future economic success. So we've got to address the problems and we're confident they can be addressed. Let's see. I need to probably let Father Crosby go next, he's been patient.
